apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata: {name: pg}
spec:
  serviceName: pg-headless
  replicas: 3
  podManagementPolicy: Parallel     # Patroni, not start order, decides who bootstraps
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg, cluster-name: pg-rw}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg, cluster-name: pg-rw}
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: pg
      enableServiceLinks: false
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 999
        runAsGroup: 999
        fsGroup: 999                # lets UID 999 read the TLS key (0440). local-path PGDATA is unaffected (S3)
        fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch
        seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}
      # ADR-001: agents only, one member per node, even spread.
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            nodeSelectorTerms:
              - matchExpressions: [{key: pg-ha/role, operator: In, values: [db]}]
        podAntiAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
              labelSelector:
                matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg, cluster-name: pg-rw}
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 1
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
          whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg, cluster-name: pg-rw}
      containers:
        - name: postgres
          image: __PG_IMAGE__
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          args: [/etc/patroni/conf.d]
          ports:
            - {name: postgresql, containerPort: 5432}
            - {name: patroni, containerPort: 8008}
          env:
            - {name: HOME, value: /tmp}
            - name: PATRONI_NAME
              valueFrom: {fieldRef: {fieldPath: metadata.name}}
            - name: PATRONI_KUBERNETES_NAMESPACE
              valueFrom: {fieldRef: {fieldPath: metadata.namespace}}
            - name: PATRONI_KUBERNETES_POD_IP
              valueFrom: {fieldRef: {fieldPath: status.podIP}}
            - {name: PATRONI_RESTAPI_CONNECT_ADDRESS, value: "$(PATRONI_KUBERNETES_POD_IP):8008"}
            - {name: PATRONI_POSTGRESQL_CONNECT_ADDRESS, value: "$(PATRONI_NAME).pg-headless.$(PATRONI_KUBERNETES_NAMESPACE).svc.cluster.local:5432"}
            - {name: PATRONI_SUPERUSER_USERNAME, value: postgres}
            - name: PATRONI_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD
              valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-postgres-password}}
            - {name: PATRONI_REPLICATION_USERNAME, value: replicator}
            - name: PATRONI_REPLICATION_PASSWORD
              valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-replicator-password}}
            - {name: PATRONI_REWIND_USERNAME, value: rewind}
            - name: PATRONI_REWIND_PASSWORD
              valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-rewind-password}}
            # Used once by post-bootstrap.sh to create the remaining roles.
            - name: PG_MONITOR_PASSWORD
              valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-monitor-password}}
            - name: PG_BACKUP_PASSWORD
              valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-backup-password}}
            - name: PG_APP_PASSWORD
              valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-app-password}}
            - name: PG_APP_RO_PASSWORD
              valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-app_ro-password}}
          # L3: archive-push and archive-get read the repository credentials and cipher passphrase from here.
          envFrom:
            - secretRef: {name: pgbackrest-repo}
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /readiness, port: 8008}
            periodSeconds: 3
            timeoutSeconds: 2
            failureThreshold: 2
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /liveness, port: 8008}
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 10
            timeoutSeconds: 3
            failureThreshold: 6
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 256Mi}
            limits: {memory: 1Gi}
          volumeMounts:
            - {name: data, mountPath: /data}
            - {name: patroni-config, mountPath: /etc/patroni/conf.d, readOnly: true}
            - {name: scripts, mountPath: /etc/patroni/scripts, readOnly: true}
            - {name: tls, mountPath: /etc/pg-tls, readOnly: true}
            - {name: pgbackrest-config, mountPath: /etc/pgbackrest, readOnly: true}
            - {name: run, mountPath: /var/run/postgresql}
            - {name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}
        # L3 (ADR-009): pgBackRest TLS server, so the stanza and backup Jobs reach this member without exec.
        # It reads PGDATA and talks to Postgres over the shared socket. It never touches the repository.
        - name: pgbackrest
          image: __PG_IMAGE__
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          command: [pgbackrest, server]
          ports:
            - {name: pgbackrest, containerPort: 8432}
          env:
            - {name: HOME, value: /tmp}
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 20m, memory: 32Mi}
            limits: {memory: 256Mi}
          volumeMounts:
            - {name: data, mountPath: /data}
            - {name: pgbackrest-server-config, mountPath: /etc/pgbackrest, readOnly: true}
            - {name: pgbackrest-tls, mountPath: /etc/pgbackrest-tls, readOnly: true}
            - {name: run, mountPath: /var/run/postgresql}
            - {name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}
      volumes:
        - name: patroni-config
          configMap: {name: pg-patroni}
        - name: scripts
          configMap: {name: pg-scripts, defaultMode: 0555}
        - name: tls
          secret: {secretName: pg-tls, defaultMode: 0440}
        - name: pgbackrest-config
          configMap:
            name: pg-pgbackrest
            items:
              - {key: db.conf, path: pgbackrest.conf}
              - {key: repo.conf, path: conf.d/repo.conf}
        # The TLS server gets no repo.conf: it never reads the repository, and so never needs its credentials.
        - name: pgbackrest-server-config
          configMap:
            name: pg-pgbackrest
            items:
              - {key: db.conf, path: pgbackrest.conf}
        - name: pgbackrest-tls
          secret: {secretName: pgbackrest-tls, defaultMode: 0440}
        - {name: run, emptyDir: {}}
        - {name: tmp, emptyDir: {}}
  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - metadata: {name: data}
      spec:
        accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
        storageClassName: local-path
        resources: {requests: {storage: 5Gi}}   # ADR-005
# L1: Patroni-managed Postgres (ADR-001..008). Rendered by scripts/deploy.sh, which fills in the image.
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: pg-ha
resources:
  - namespace.yaml
  - rbac.yaml
  - services.yaml
  - statefulset.yaml
  - pdb.yaml
  - backup-cronjob.yaml
  - restore-test-cronjob.yaml
configMapGenerator:
  # Patroni reads every file in /etc/patroni/conf.d, merged in name order.
  # L3 adds archiving as 20-archive.yml without editing 10-base.yml.
  - name: pg-patroni
    files: [patroni/10-base.yml, patroni/20-archive.yml]
  # ADR-009: repo.conf holds every repo1-* setting; db.conf and job.conf hold the rest.
  - name: pg-pgbackrest
    files: [pgbackrest/repo.conf, pgbackrest/db.conf, pgbackrest/job.conf, pgbackrest/restore-test.conf]
  - name: pg-scripts
    files: [scripts/post-bootstrap.sh, scripts/backup-job.sh, scripts/restore-bootstrap.sh, scripts/restore-test.sh, scripts/fingerprint.sql]
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: pg-ha
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version: v1.35
# Stable pod DNS names (pg-N.pg-headless.pg-ha.svc), which the L0 server certificate covers.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: pg-headless}
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  publishNotReadyAddresses: true   # members must resolve each other while bootstrapping
  selector: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg, cluster-name: pg-rw}
  ports:
    - {name: postgresql, port: 5432}
    - {name: patroni, port: 8008}
---
# ADR-007: no selector. Patroni writes the leader into Endpoints pg-rw, mirrored to an EndpointSlice.
# The Endpoints object is deliberately not declared here, so re-applying never overwrites the lock.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: pg-rw}
spec:
  ports:
    - {name: postgresql, port: 5432, targetPort: 5432}
---
# ADR-007: ready replicas only. Patroni maintains the role label.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: pg-ro}
spec:
  selector: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg, cluster-name: pg-rw, role: replica}
  ports:
    - {name: postgresql, port: 5432}
# ADR-002: least privilege for Patroni's Kubernetes DCS with use_endpoints.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata: {name: pg}
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata: {name: pg-patroni}
rules:
  # Leader lock, config, sync and failover keys live in Endpoints pg-rw, pg-rw-config, pg-rw-sync, pg-rw-failover.
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: [endpoints]
    verbs: [get, list, watch, create, update, patch, delete]
  # Member state is stored as pod annotations, and the role label drives pg-ro.
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: [pods]
    verbs: [get, list, watch, update, patch]
  # Patroni creates a headless Service for pg-rw-config so the Endpoints controller never removes it.
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: [services]
    verbs: [create]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata: {name: pg-patroni}
roleRef: {apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io, kind: Role, name: pg-patroni}
subjects:
  - {kind: ServiceAccount, name: pg}

# Patroni L1 base config. Per-pod values (name, addresses, passwords) come from environment variables.
# L3 adds archive_mode, archive_command and restore_command in a later file (20-archive.yml), which
# Patroni merges over this one.
scope: pg-rw            # Patroni names the leader Endpoints after the scope, so this is the pg-rw Service
restapi:
  listen: 0.0.0.0:8008
kubernetes:             # ADR-002
  use_endpoints: true
  labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg, cluster-name: pg-rw}
  role_label: role
  ports: [{name: postgresql, port: 5432}]
bootstrap:
  dcs:
    ttl: 20             # ADR-006: loop_wait + 2 x retry_timeout = 13 s < ttl
    loop_wait: 3
    retry_timeout: 5
    primary_start_timeout: 0
    maximum_lag_on_failover: 1048576
    synchronous_mode: true          # ADR-004: non-strict, one synchronous standby
    synchronous_mode_strict: false
    synchronous_node_count: 1
    postgresql:
      use_pg_rewind: false          # ADR-008 (L3): rejoin by re-clone, see remove_data_directory_on_diverged_timelines
      use_slots: true               # ADR-005
      parameters:
        wal_level: replica
        hot_standby: "on"
        wal_log_hints: "on"         # ADR-008, in addition to data checksums
        max_wal_size: 512MB         # ADR-005
        max_slot_wal_keep_size: 1GB # ADR-005: hard cap on WAL held for slots
        max_wal_senders: 10
        max_replication_slots: 10
        max_connections: 100
        shared_buffers: 128MB
        password_encryption: scram-sha-256
  initdb:
    - data-checksums
    - encoding: UTF8
  post_bootstrap: /etc/patroni/scripts/post-bootstrap.sh
postgresql:
  listen: 0.0.0.0:5432

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs one Job from the pg-backup CronJob template (or CRONJOB=pg-restore-test, L4) and waits for it. No exec (D4).
#   [CRONJOB=name] scripts/pgbr-job.sh NAME [COMMAND] [ENV=VALUE...]
# Without COMMAND (or with an empty one) the Job runs the CronJob's own backup script, as make backup does.
# Prints the Job's log, and exits non-zero if the Job failed.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
name=$1; cmd=${2:-}; shift; [ $# -eq 0 ] || shift
envs=$(printf '%s\n' "$@" | jq -Rn '[inputs | select(length > 0) | split("=") | {name: .[0], value: (.[1:] | join("="))}]')
kubectl -n "$PG_NS" delete job "$name" --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null
kubectl -n "$PG_NS" create job "$name" --from=cronjob/${CRONJOB:-pg-backup} --dry-run=client -o json |
  jq --arg cmd "$cmd" --argjson envs "$envs" '
    .spec.template.spec.containers[0] |= ((if $cmd == "" then . else .command = ["bash", "-ec", $cmd] end) | .env += $envs)' |
  kubectl -n "$PG_NS" apply -f - >/dev/null
end=$((SECONDS + ${JOB_WAIT:-1800}))
while :; do
  s=$(kubectl -n "$PG_NS" get job "$name" -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}/{.status.failed}' 2>/dev/null || true)
  [ "${s%/*}" = 1 ] || [ "${s#*/}" = 1 ] && break
  [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || { s=timeout; break; }
  sleep 2
done
kubectl -n "$PG_NS" logs "job/$name" 2>/dev/null || true
[ "${s%/*}" = 1 ]

The calls run in the order sent, so the publish carries the edited file; a publish sent in the same response as a failed Edit of that file is refused and leaves the artifact as it was, so correct the Edit and publish again. Either way, read the file first only if its text is not in this conversation or you can't place the change exactly from it.

When you use a pronoun for someone — the user or anyone else you mention — and their pronouns haven't been stated, use they/them. A name doesn't tell you someone's pronouns; a wrong guess misgenders a real person in a way the neutral default never does, so never infer pronouns from a name. For actions that are hard to reverse or outward-facing, confirm first unless durably authorized or explicitly told to proceed without asking; approval in one context doesn't extend to the next.
