tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. The cache is positional: agent() calls replay from cache up to the first call that failed, no longer matches the earlier run (edited, added, removed or reordered) or never started in it; that call and every call after it run again, even when their own (prompt, opts) are unchanged. A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

# L4 restore: history and notes

This file is maintained by hand. The L4 tests write only [`L4-restore.md`](L4-restore.md) and the files in [`L4/`](L4/), and never touch this file. Times are UTC, on 2026-11-25. L4 started at 15:21.

## Before L4: the two L2/L3 gaps

- **Step 0a (15:21 to 15:25):** the third, authorised run of `make failover-chain` passed and wrote `L2/chain.md`.
- **Step 0b (15:28 to 15:32):** `make failover-diverge` forced a divergence on the first attempt. The old primary rejoined by re-clone, was switched back to leader, and archived with no failures. Details are in [`L2-failover-history.md`](L2-failover-history.md).

## Design points settled during implementation

- **`post_bootstrap` runs after a custom bootstrap too.** Patroni 4.1.5 calls it after a restore, so `CREATE ROLE` would have failed on the restored roles. `post-bootstrap.sh` is now create-or-alter, which also resets the restored passwords to the target namespace's Secret (ADR-010).
- **Recovery settings stay out of `postgresql.auto.conf`.** pgBackRest writes `restore_command` and the recovery target there. Replicas cloned from the restored primary would copy those lines, and they would outlive the end of recovery. `restore-bootstrap.sh` removes them after the restore, and Patroni's `recovery_conf` drives recovery instead.
- **The restored cluster cannot archive into the source stanza.** `30-restore.yml` sets `archive_mode: "off"`. The full-restore test checks that the setting is off, that the restored primary's archiver counters are zero, and that the source archive has no WAL directory for the restored timeline.
- **Data check for the restore test.** The backup Job records a fingerprint as pgBackRest annotations: row counts and `hashtext` sums of the seeded pgbench tables, read as `app_ro` through `pg-rw` just before the backup. The restore test compares it after a `--type=immediate` restore. The tables only change on `make seed`, so a backup taken while the probe writes elsewhere still matches.
  - **Limit:** this fingerprints test data. A production deployment would choose its own marker tables.
  - On a cluster that was never seeded, the fingerprint is `seeded=no`, which the restore test still compares.

## What failed on the way

1. **Full restore, first attempt (15:33).** A test bug: the test library exports `NS=pg-ha`, and `scripts/restore.sh` reads `NS`, so it correctly refused to restore into the source namespace. Nothing was created or deleted, and `restore-clean` also refused `pg-ha`. The tests now pass `NS=pg-restore` explicitly. The second attempt passed.
2. **Restore test, first attempt (15:42).** `FATAL: recovery aborted because of insufficient parameter settings`. The scratch config set `max_connections = 20`, and recovery requires at least the primary's value (100). The Job failed loudly, as designed. `max_connections` is back at its default, and the second attempt passed. The rest of that sequence (the negative run and the scheduled capture) was stopped, so their attempts were not spent on a known failure.
3. **A blocked command.** A safety check blocked one shell command that created several files through heredocs, because the embedded scripts contained `rm -f`. Nothing in it ran. The two test scripts were then written with the editor instead.

## PITR: B was first committed too early

The first PITR run passed, but marker B was committed 18.5 s after T, once A's segment had been archived, not after `archive_timeout` as the brief says. The proof itself held: Postgres logged `recovery stopping before commit of transaction 4595`, which is B's commit. The test now waits at least 65 s after T before committing B. The rerun (15:44 to 15:46) passed: B was committed 66.0 s after T, Postgres logged `recovery stopping before commit of transaction 4608` (B), and the restore took 27.99 s end to end. The rerun replaced the first run's evidence file. Both runs' log lines are quoted here.

## PITR across timelines (R5.5, observed)

pgBackRest picks the newest backup that ends before the target. In the first PITR run (target `2026-11-25 21:39:28+06`), that was `20261125-133844F`, taken before the L2 rerun's failovers. Recovery to a target on timeline 27 therefore replayed across every timeline switch in between, using the history files in the archive, and stopped at the right transaction (`recovery stopping before commit of transaction 4595`). The rerun used the newer `20261125-154309F` on the same timeline, so its evidence file does not show this crossing. R5.5 ("a target time after a failover restores correctly") is shown by that run. There is no dedicated `T:pitr-timeline` test.

tests/failover.sh:122:      T_FAULT=$(now); docker exec "$OLD_NODE" sh -c "nsenter -t $PID -m -p -- umount -l /data && kill -KILL $PM"

tests/failover.sh:219:  storage) DESC='The primary'"'"'s data volume is made unavailable inside its container: `/data` is lazily unmounted in the Postgres container'"'"'s mount namespace (`docker exec <agent> nsenter -t <pid> -m umount -l /data`) and the postmaster is killed with SIGKILL, so Patroni cannot restart Postgres. It is restored by deleting the pod once a new leader holds the lock, so the kubelet mounts the volume again. **Limits:** a running Postgres does not notice a detached directory because it works relative to its open data directory, so the SIGKILL stands in for the I/O error or PANIC a real disk failure would cause. The data on the volume is intact, so this is not a lost or corrupted disk, and a hung disk that blocks I/O without failing is not shown. A read-only remount was tried first and refused (`mount point is busy`), because Postgres holds its files open for writing.' ;;
tests/failover.sh:220:  split-brain) DESC='An iptables rule on the primary'"'"'s node drops only the primary pod'"'"'s traffic to the API server backend (the S2 finding: policy and filtering see the real backend address). Replication and client traffic are untouched, so the old primary can still reach its sync standby and acknowledge commits until it demotes itself. The rule is removed afterwards.' ;;
tests/failover.sh:221:  diverge) DESC='Replication traffic from the primary pod to both replicas is dropped by iptables on its node for '"${DIVERGE_HOLD:-5}"' s while the probe writes, so the primary writes WAL (commits that wait for the sync standby and are never acknowledged) that no replica receives. Then its k3d agent is stopped, as in the node mode, and started again once a new leader holds the lock. RTO counts from the start of the block. The old primary has diverged and must rejoin by re-clone (ADR-008).' ;;

81:metadata: {name: garage-bootstrap}
88:      nodeSelector: {pg-ha/role: infra}
# ADR-001: 1 tainted server + 3 agents. ADR-007: node-monitor-grace-period=20s.
# The k3s image is passed by scripts/cluster.sh from versions.env.
apiVersion: k3d.io/v1alpha5
kind: Simple
metadata:
  name: pg-ha
servers: 1
agents: 3
kubeAPI:
  hostIP: 127.0.0.1
  hostPort: "6550"
options:
  k3d:
    wait: true
    timeout: 180s
    disableLoadbalancer: true   # one server, so a load balancer adds nothing
  k3s:
    extraArgs:
      - arg: --disable=traefik,servicelb,metrics-server
        nodeFilters: [server:*]
      - arg: --kube-controller-manager-arg=node-monitor-grace-period=20s
        nodeFilters: [server:*]
      - arg: --node-taint=node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane=true:NoSchedule
        nodeFilters: [server:*]
    nodeLabels:
      - label: pg-ha/role=db
        nodeFilters: [agent:*]
      - label: pg-ha/role=infra
        nodeFilters: [server:*]
  kubeconfig:
    updateDefaultKubeconfig: false   # never touch ~/.kube/config
    switchCurrentContext: false

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Spike harness: runs commands, records them with their output, and writes a PASS/FAIL evidence file.
# Any value from ./secrets/credentials is replaced by a visible placeholder before it reaches the file.
. "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../lib.sh"
SPIKE_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/scripts/spikes"
EV_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/docs/evidence"

redact() {
  python3 -I -c '
import glob, os, sys
data = sys.stdin.read()
for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "*")):
    value = open(path).read().strip()
    if value:
        data = data.replace(value, "[REDACTED:" + os.path.basename(path) + "]")
sys.stdout.write(data)' "$SECRETS_DIR/credentials"
}

ev_start() { # id title question criteria
  SPIKE=$1; TITLE=$2; QUESTION=$3; CRITERIA=$4; NS="spike-$(echo "$1" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
  BODY=$(mktemp); CHECKS=$(mktemp); FAILS=0; T0=$SECONDS; STARTED=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)
  kubectl get ns "$NS" >/dev/null 2>&1 && kubectl delete ns "$NS" --wait=true >/dev/null
  trap ev_cleanup EXIT
}
ev_cleanup() {
  [ "${KEEP:-0}" = 1 ] || kubectl delete ns "$NS" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f "$BODY" "$CHECKS"
}
section() { printf '\n## %s\n' "$1" >> "$BODY"; log "== $1"; }
run() { # command string; output is recorded. Returns the command's exit code.
  local out rc=0
  out=$(eval "$1" 2>&1) || rc=$?
  { printf '\n```console\n$ %s\n' "$1"; printf '%s\n' "$out"; [ $rc -eq 0 ] || printf '[exit code %s]\n' "$rc"; printf '```\n'; } | redact >> "$BODY"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | redact | tail -"${TAIL:-12}"
  return $rc
}
note() { printf '\n%s\n' "$1" >> "$BODY"; }
check() { # description, command...
  local d=$1; shift
  if "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '| %s | PASS |\n' "$d" >> "$CHECKS"; log "PASS  $d"
  else printf '| %s | **FAIL** |\n' "$d" >> "$CHECKS"; log "FAIL  $d"; FAILS=$((FAILS+1)); fi
}
ev_finish() {
  local verdict=PASS; [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ] || verdict=FAIL
  local f="$EV_DIR/L0-spike-$SPIKE.md"; mkdir -p "$EV_DIR"
  { printf '# L0 spike %s: %s\n\n**Result: %s**\n\n' "$SPIKE" "$TITLE" "$verdict"
    printf -- '- **Question:** %s\n- **Pass criteria:** %s\n' "$QUESTION" "$CRITERIA"
    printf -- '- **Run:** %s (UTC), %s s\n- **Reproduce:** `make spike-%s`\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))" "$(echo "$SPIKE" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
    printf -- '- **Versions:** k3s `%s`, image `%s`\n' "${K3S_IMAGE%@*}" "$PG_IMAGE"
    [ ! -f "$EV_DIR/L0-spike-$SPIKE-history.md" ] || printf -- '- **History:** [`L0-spike-%s-history.md`](L0-spike-%s-history.md) (maintained by hand, never written by this harness)\n' "$SPIKE" "$SPIKE"
    printf '\n## Checks\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n'; cat "$CHECKS"; cat "$BODY"; } | redact > "$f"
  log "RESULT $SPIKE: $verdict -> docs/evidence/L0-spike-$SPIKE.md"
  [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]
}
wait_job() { # job timeout-seconds; succeeds only if the Job completes
  local end=$((SECONDS+$2)) s f
  while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do
    s=$(kubectl -n "$NS" get job "$1" -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}' 2>/dev/null || true)
    f=$(kubectl -n "$NS" get job "$1" -o jsonpath='{.status.failed}' 2>/dev/null || true)
    [ "${s:-0}" -ge 1 ] && return 0; [ "${f:-0}" -ge 1 ] && return 1; sleep 1
  done; return 1
}
apply_yaml() { sed "s|__IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|g; s|__NS__|$NS|g" | kubectl -n "$NS" apply -f - ; }
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the L4 restore tests. Each test writes docs/evidence/L4/<part>.md, then regenerates
# docs/evidence/L4-restore.md. SQL runs in the test client pod in pg-ha (no exec in a Postgres pod); it
# reaches the restored cluster through its pg-rw Service in pg-restore. Repository reads run in Jobs.
. "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/l3-lib.sh"
mkdir -p "$EV_DIR/L4"
RNS=pg-restore; RRW=pg-rw.$RNS.svc.cluster.local
# The data fingerprint of fingerprint.sql (seeded branch), as one statement for the test client.
FP_SQL="select 'rows.pgbench_accounts=' || count(*) from pgbench_accounts
union all select 'sum.pgbench_accounts=' || sum(hashtext(a::text)::bigint) from pgbench_accounts a
union all select 'rows.pgbench_branches=' || count(*) from pgbench_branches
union all select 'sum.pgbench_branches=' || sum(hashtext(b::text)::bigint) from pgbench_branches b
union all select 'rows.pgbench_tellers=' || count(*) from pgbench_tellers
union all select 'sum.pgbench_tellers=' || sum(hashtext(t::text)::bigint) from pgbench_tellers t"
rpatroni() { local i; for i in 0 1 2; do kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/namespaces/$RNS/pods/pg-$i:8008/proxy/cluster" 2>/dev/null && return 0; done; return 1; }
rleader() { rpatroni | jq -r '.members[] | select(.role == "leader") | .name'; }
# History files in the repository archive, from a short Job (repo-ls). Prints one name per line.
repo_history() { local j=pg-repo-ls-$RANDOM o; o=$(pgbr "$j" 'pgbackrest --stanza=main --output=text repo-ls archive/main/17-1') || true
  kubectl -n "$NS" delete job "$j" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; grep -E '^[0-9A-F]{8}\.history$' <<<"$o" || true; }
repo_wal_dirs() { local j=pg-repo-ls-$RANDOM o; o=$(pgbr "$j" 'pgbackrest --stanza=main --output=text repo-ls archive/main/17-1') || true
  kubectl -n "$NS" delete job "$j" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; grep -E '^[0-9A-F]{16}$' <<<"$o" || true; }

l4_finish() { # part title description make-target
  local verdict=PASS; [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ] || verdict=FAIL
  { printf '# L4: %s\n\n**Result: %s**\n\n' "$2" "$verdict"
    printf -- '- **What:** %s\n' "$3"
    printf -- '- **Run:** %s (UTC), %s s\n- **Reproduce:** `make %s`\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))" "$4"
    printf -- '- **Versions:** k3s `%s`, image `%s`, Garage `%s`\n' "${K3S_IMAGE%%@*}" "$PG_IMAGE" "${GARAGE_IMAGE%%@*}"
    [ ! -f "$EV_DIR/L4-restore-history.md" ] || printf -- '- **History:** [`L4-restore-history.md`](../L4-restore-history.md) (maintained by hand)\n'
    printf '\n## Checks\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n'; cat "$CHECKS"; cat "$BODY"; } | redact > "$EV_DIR/L4/$1.md"
  "$ROOT_DIR/tests/l4-summary.sh"
  log "RESULT L4 $1: $verdict -> docs/evidence/L4/$1.md"
  rm -f "$BODY" "$CHECKS"
  [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]
}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regenerates docs/evidence/L4-restore.md from the per-part files in docs/evidence/L4/.
. "$(dirname "$0")/../scripts/spikes/lib.sh"
PARTS="restore-full:Full restore into an empty namespace (R5.1)
pitr:Point-in-time recovery (R5.3)
restore-test:Restore test Job, on demand (R4.5, R5.4)
restore-scheduled:Restore test Job, scheduled (R4.5)"
{ printf '# L4: restore, PITR and restore verification\n\nGenerated from the per-part files in [`L4/`](L4/) each time a part runs. Timestamps are UTC.\n\n'
  [ ! -f "$EV_DIR/L4-restore-history.md" ] || printf 'Hand-written notes: [`L4-restore-history.md`](L4-restore-history.md).\n\n'
  printf '| Part | Result | Checks passed | Details |\n|---|---|---:|---|\n'
  while IFS=: read -r f t; do
    if [ -f "$EV_DIR/L4/$f.md" ]; then
      r=$(grep -m1 -oE 'Result: (PASS|FAIL)' "$EV_DIR/L4/$f.md" | cut -d' ' -f2)
      p=$(grep -c '| PASS |$' "$EV_DIR/L4/$f.md" || true); n=$(grep -cE '\| (PASS|\*\*FAIL\*\*) \|$' "$EV_DIR/L4/$f.md" || true)
      printf '| %s | %s | %s of %s | [`L4/%s.md`](L4/%s.md) |\n' "$t" "$r" "$p" "$n" "$f" "$f"
    else printf '| %s | Not run yet | | |\n' "$t"; fi
  done <<<"$PARTS"
  while IFS=: read -r f t; do
    [ -f "$EV_DIR/L4/$f.md" ] || continue
    printf '\n## %s\n\n' "$t"; sed -n '/^- \*\*What:\*\*/p' "$EV_DIR/L4/$f.md"; printf '\n'
    sed -n '/^## Checks/,/^## /p' "$EV_DIR/L4/$f.md" | sed '1,2d' | grep '^|'
  done <<<"$PARTS"; } > "$EV_DIR/L4-restore.md"

# L5 (ADR-011): custom postgres_exporter queries, read by the exporter sidecar of each member.
# Each query works on a primary and on a standby. pg_current_wal_lsn() is only called when not in
# recovery, because it raises an error on a standby. The monitor role has pg_monitor, which covers
# pg_stat_replication, pg_replication_slots and pg_ls_archive_statusdir().

# WAL waiting to be archived (L4 phase notes). A .ready file is created when a segment is complete, so the
# age of the oldest one is how long finished WAL has waited for the repository. On a quiet primary nothing
# is written, no segment is closed and no .ready file exists, so this does not grow on an idle cluster
# (pg_stat_archiver.last_archived_time does).
pg_ha_archive:
  query: |
    select count(*) filter (where name like '%.ready') as ready_count,
           coalesce(extract(epoch from now() - min(modification) filter (where name like '%.ready')), 0) as oldest_ready_seconds
    from pg_ls_archive_statusdir()
  metrics:
    - ready_count: {usage: GAUGE, description: "WAL segments waiting to be archived (.ready files)"}
    - oldest_ready_seconds: {usage: GAUGE, description: "Age in seconds of the oldest .ready file, 0 when none"}

# Replication lag per standby as seen by the primary (R1.7). Bytes: WAL the primary has written that the
# standby has not replayed yet. Seconds: replay_lag, which Postgres reports as NULL once a standby has
# caught up and nothing new is written, so NULL becomes 0. Empty on a standby.
pg_ha_replication:
  query: |
    select application_name, state, sync_state,
           case when pg_is_in_recovery() then 0 else pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), replay_lsn) end as lag_bytes,
           coalesce(extract(epoch from replay_lag), 0) as replay_lag_seconds
    from pg_stat_replication
    where replay_lsn is not null
  metrics:
    - application_name: {usage: LABEL, description: "Standby name (the Patroni member name)"}
    - state: {usage: LABEL, description: "walsender state"}
    - sync_state: {usage: LABEL, description: "sync or async"}
    - lag_bytes: {usage: GAUGE, description: "Bytes between the primary's current WAL position and the standby's replay position"}
    - replay_lag_seconds: {usage: GAUGE, description: "pg_stat_replication.replay_lag in seconds, 0 when caught up"}

# WAL held back by each replication slot (R1.6, ADR-005). On a standby, the reference is the replay position.
# lost = 1 when Postgres has invalidated the slot because it passed max_slot_wal_keep_size.
pg_ha_slot:
  query: |
    select slot_name, slot_type,
           active::int as active,
           (wal_status = 'lost')::int as lost,
           coalesce(pg_wal_lsn_diff(case when pg_is_in_recovery() then pg_last_wal_replay_lsn() else pg_current_wal_lsn() end, restart_lsn), 0) as retained_bytes,
           coalesce(safe_wal_size, 0) as safe_wal_size_bytes
    from pg_replication_slots
  metrics:
    - slot_name: {usage: LABEL, description: "Slot name"}
    - slot_type: {usage: LABEL, description: "physical or logical"}
    - active: {usage: GAUGE, description: "1 when a walsender is using the slot"}
    - lost: {usage: GAUGE, description: "1 when wal_status is lost"}
    - retained_bytes: {usage: GAUGE, description: "WAL bytes the slot keeps from being removed"}
    - safe_wal_size_bytes: {usage: GAUGE, description: "Bytes that can still be written before the slot is lost"}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deploys Garage (L3), the Patroni cluster (L1) with WAL archiving (L3), and creates the pgBackRest stanza.
# Waits until healthy. Idempotent, and never prints a secret.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
cluster_exists || die "cluster $CLUSTER_NAME not found, run: make cluster"
C="$SECRETS_DIR/credentials"; T="$SECRETS_DIR/tls"
for f in "$C"/pg-{postgres,replicator,rewind,monitor,backup,app,app_ro}-password \
         "$T"/{ca.crt,postgres-server.crt,postgres-server.key,pgbackrest-server.crt,pgbackrest-server.key,pgbackrest-client.crt,pgbackrest-client.key}; do
  [ -s "$f" ] || die "missing $f, run: make certs secrets"
done
BACKUP_SCHEDULE=${BACKUP_SCHEDULE:-0 20 * * *}   # ADR-009: daily at 20:00 UTC unless overridden
[[ "$BACKUP_SCHEDULE" =~ ^[0-9*/,-]+( [0-9*/,-]+){4}$ ]] || die "BACKUP_SCHEDULE must be a 5-field cron expression"
RESTORE_TEST_SCHEDULE=${RESTORE_TEST_SCHEDULE:-0 21 * * *}   # ADR-010: daily, after the backup
[[ "$RESTORE_TEST_SCHEDULE" =~ ^[0-9*/,-]+( [0-9*/,-]+){4}$ ]] || die "RESTORE_TEST_SCHEDULE must be a 5-field cron expression"

# ADR-001: cluster DNS is infrastructure, so it runs on the server node with Garage, never on a database
# node. k3s schedules its single CoreDNS replica anywhere. When that was the primary's node, a node failure
# took DNS down with it, and the promoted standby sat in restore_command (archive-get resolving Garage) until
# DNS returned (L3, docs/evidence/L3-backup-history.md). k3s re-applies its addon manifest with a three-way
# merge, which keeps this added nodeSelector key.
kubectl -n kube-system patch deployment coredns --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"nodeSelector":{"pg-ha/role":"infra"}}}}}' >/dev/null
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deployment/coredns --timeout=120s >/dev/null

# L3: Garage first, so WAL archiving has somewhere to go as soon as Postgres starts (ADR-014).
"$ROOT_DIR/scripts/garage.sh"

kubectl apply -f "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/pg/namespace.yaml" >/dev/null
# Server-side apply keeps secret values out of the last-applied annotation.
secret() { kubectl -n "$PG_NS" create secret generic "$@" --dry-run=client -o yaml |
  kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager=pg-ha-deploy --force-conflicts -f - >/dev/null; }
secret pg-credentials $(for r in postgres replicator rewind monitor backup app app_ro; do printf -- '--from-file=%s ' "$C/pg-$r-password"; done)
secret pg-tls --from-file=tls.crt="$T/postgres-server.crt" --from-file=tls.key="$T/postgres-server.key" --from-file=ca.crt="$T/ca.crt"
secret pgbackrest-tls --from-file=server.crt="$T/pgbackrest-server.crt" --from-file=server.key="$T/pgbackrest-server.key" \
  --from-file=client.crt="$T/pgbackrest-client.crt" --from-file=client.key="$T/pgbackrest-client.key" --from-file=ca.crt="$T/ca.crt"
kubectl kustomize "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/pg" | sed "s|__PG_IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|; s|__BACKUP_SCHEDULE__|'$BACKUP_SCHEDULE'|; s|__RESTORE_TEST_SCHEDULE__|'$RESTORE_TEST_SCHEDULE'|" | kubectl apply -f -

kubectl -n "$PG_NS" rollout status "statefulset/$PG_STS" --timeout=600s
end=$((SECONDS + ${PG_WAIT:-180}))
until patroni_healthy; do
  [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || { patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | "\(.name) \(.role) \(.state)"' || true; die "Patroni not healthy after ${PG_WAIT:-180} s"; }
  sleep 2
done
log "Patroni healthy: 1 leader, 2 streaming replicas, 1 sync standby"

# L3: create the stanza (idempotent), then prove that archiving reaches the repository.
out=$(JOB_WAIT=300 "$ROOT_DIR/scripts/pgbr-job.sh" pg-stanza-create \
  'pgbackrest --stanza=main --log-level-console=info stanza-create && pgbackrest --stanza=main --log-level-console=info check && echo STANZA_OK') ||
  { printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -20; die "stanza-create or check failed"; }
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E 'stanza-create command end|check command end|already exists|STANZA_OK' || true

# L5 (ADR-011): custom postgres_exporter queries, read by the exporter sidecar of each member.
# Each query works on a primary and on a standby. pg_current_wal_lsn() is only called when not in
# recovery, because it raises an error on a standby. The monitor role has pg_monitor, which covers
# pg_stat_replication, pg_replication_slots and pg_ls_archive_statusdir().

# WAL waiting to be archived (L4 phase notes). A .ready file is created when a segment is complete, so the
# age of the oldest one is how long finished WAL has waited for the repository. On a quiet primary nothing
# is written, no segment is closed and no .ready file exists, so this does not grow on an idle cluster
# (pg_stat_archiver.last_archived_time does).
pg_ha_archive:
  query: |
    select count(*) filter (where name like '%.ready') as ready_count,
           coalesce(extract(epoch from now() - min(modification) filter (where name like '%.ready')), 0) as oldest_ready_seconds
    from pg_ls_archive_statusdir()
  metrics:
    - ready_count: {usage: GAUGE, description: "WAL segments waiting to be archived (.ready files)"}
    - oldest_ready_seconds: {usage: GAUGE, description: "Age in seconds of the oldest .ready file, 0 when none"}

# Replication lag per standby as seen by the primary (R1.7). Bytes: WAL the primary has written that the
# standby has not replayed yet. Seconds: replay_lag, which Postgres reports as NULL once a standby has
# caught up and nothing new is written, so NULL becomes 0. Empty on a standby.
pg_ha_replication:
  query: |
    select application_name, state, sync_state,
           case when pg_is_in_recovery() then 0 else pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), replay_lsn) end as lag_bytes,
           coalesce(extract(epoch from replay_lag), 0) as replay_lag_seconds
    from pg_stat_replication
    where replay_lsn is not null
  metrics:
    - application_name: {usage: LABEL, description: "Standby name (the Patroni member name)"}
    - state: {usage: LABEL, description: "walsender state"}
    - sync_state: {usage: LABEL, description: "sync or async"}
    - lag_bytes: {usage: GAUGE, description: "Bytes between the primary's current WAL position and the standby's replay position"}
    - replay_lag_seconds: {usage: GAUGE, description: "pg_stat_replication.replay_lag in seconds, 0 when caught up"}

# WAL held back by each replication slot (R1.6, ADR-005). On a standby, the reference is the replay position.
# lost = 1 when Postgres has invalidated the slot because it passed max_slot_wal_keep_size.
pg_ha_slot:
  query: |
    select slot_name, slot_type,
           active::int as active,
           (wal_status = 'lost')::int as lost,
           coalesce(pg_wal_lsn_diff(case when pg_is_in_recovery() then pg_last_wal_replay_lsn() else pg_current_wal_lsn() end, restart_lsn), 0) as retained_bytes,
           coalesce(safe_wal_size, 0) as safe_wal_size_bytes
    from pg_replication_slots
  metrics:
    - slot_name: {usage: LABEL, description: "Slot name"}
    - slot_type: {usage: LABEL, description: "physical or logical"}
    - active: {usage: GAUGE, description: "1 when a walsender is using the slot"}
    - lost: {usage: GAUGE, description: "1 when wal_status is lost"}
    - retained_bytes: {usage: GAUGE, description: "WAL bytes the slot keeps from being removed"}
    - safe_wal_size_bytes: {usage: GAUGE, description: "Bytes that can still be written before the slot is lost"}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L4 (ADR-010, R5.1, R5.3): restores the whole cluster from the pgBackRest repository into an empty namespace,
# through Patroni's custom bootstrap (deploy/restore). The first member restores and recovers, the other two
# clone from it, so the result is 1 primary and 2 streaming replicas, as in production.
#   NS=pg-restore              target namespace. The L0 certificates cover only pg-ha and pg-restore.
#   TARGET_TIME='YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS+06'   point in time, with a REQUIRED timezone offset. Empty: latest.
#   TARGET_TIMELINE=latest     recovery target timeline (default latest).
# The restored cluster never archives into the source stanza: archive_mode is off (30-restore.yml), and it
# reads the repository only through restore_command. Never prints a secret.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
SRC_NS=$PG_NS; NS=${NS:-pg-restore}; TARGET_TIME=${TARGET_TIME:-}; TARGET_TIMELINE=${TARGET_TIMELINE:-latest}
[ "$NS" != "$SRC_NS" ] || die "refusing to restore into the source namespace $SRC_NS"
[ "$NS" = pg-restore ] || die "NS must be pg-restore: the L0 certificates name only pg-ha and pg-restore"
if [ -n "$TARGET_TIME" ]; then
  [[ "$TARGET_TIME" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\ [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(\.[0-9]+)?[+-][0-9]{2}(:?[0-9]{2})?$ ]] ||
    die "TARGET_TIME must look like '2026-11-26 01:30:00+06', with a timezone offset (the VM runs UTC, the lead works in UTC+6)"
fi
[[ "$TARGET_TIMELINE" =~ ^(latest|current|[0-9]+)$ ]] || die "TARGET_TIMELINE must be latest, current or a number"
if kubectl get ns "$NS" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  [ -z "$(kubectl -n "$NS" get pods,pvc -o name 2>/dev/null)" ] || die "namespace $NS is not empty, run: make restore-clean"
fi
T0=$(date +%s.%N)
log "Restoring into namespace $NS: target ${TARGET_TIME:-latest (end of the archive)}, timeline $TARGET_TIMELINE"

kubectl create ns "$NS" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null
# Same Secrets as the source namespace, copied server-side so no value is printed or stored in an annotation.
for s in pg-credentials pg-tls pgbackrest-tls pgbackrest-repo; do
  kubectl -n "$SRC_NS" get secret "$s" -o json | jq --arg s "$s" '{apiVersion, kind, type, data, metadata: {name: $s}}' |
    kubectl -n "$NS" apply --server-side --field-manager=pg-ha-restore --force-conflicts -f - >/dev/null
done

# 30-restore.yml: Patroni custom bootstrap through pgBackRest, merged over 10-base.yml and 20-archive.yml.
q() { printf "'%s'" "$1"; }
{ echo "# Generated by scripts/restore.sh at $(date -u +%FT%TZ). Do not edit or commit."
  echo "bootstrap:"
  echo "  method: pgbackrest"
  echo "  pgbackrest:"
  echo "    command: \"sh /etc/patroni/scripts/restore-bootstrap.sh $(q "$TARGET_TIME") $(q "$TARGET_TIMELINE")\""
  echo "    no_params: true"
  echo "    recovery_conf:"
  echo "      restore_command: pgbackrest --stanza=main archive-get %f \"%p\""
  echo "      recovery_target_timeline: $(q "$TARGET_TIMELINE")"
  echo "      recovery_target_action: promote"
  [ -z "$TARGET_TIME" ] || echo "      recovery_target_time: $(q "$TARGET_TIME")"
  echo "postgresql:"
  echo "  parameters:"
  echo "    archive_mode: \"off\"   # ADR-010: never archive into the source stanza"
} > "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/restore/30-restore.yml"
kubectl kustomize "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/restore" | sed "s|__PG_IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|" | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null

PG_NS=$NS   # the Patroni helpers below now read the restored cluster
end=$((SECONDS + ${RESTORE_WAIT:-1200})); T_LEADER=""
until [ -n "$T_LEADER" ] && patroni_healthy; do
  [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || { patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | "\(.name) \(.role) \(.state)"' || true; die "restored cluster not healthy after ${RESTORE_WAIT:-1200} s"; }
  [ -n "$T_LEADER" ] || ! patroni_cluster 2>/dev/null | jq -e '[.members[] | select(.role == "leader" and .state == "running")] | length == 1' >/dev/null || T_LEADER=$(date +%s.%N)
  sleep 2
done
T1=$(date +%s.%N)
patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | "  \(.name) \(.role) \(.state) timeline \(.timeline // "-")"'
log "RESTORE_OK namespace=$NS target=${TARGET_TIME:-latest} primary_ready=$(awk -v a="$T0" -v b="$T_LEADER" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", b-a}')s cluster_healthy=$(awk -v a="$T0" -v b="$T1" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", b-a}')s"

lines: echo "    archive_mode: \"off\"   # ADR-010: never archive into the source stanza"
PG_NS=$NS   # the Patroni helpers below now read the restored cluster

# L5 (ADR-011). Two namespaces so that only node_exporter runs outside the restricted Pod Security profile.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: monitoring
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version: v1.35
---
# Documented Pod Security exception (R8.7, ADR-011): node_exporter needs a read-only hostPath mount of the
# node's root filesystem to report disk space. hostPath is forbidden by both baseline and restricted, so this
# namespace enforces privileged. It holds node_exporter only. The pod still runs as non-root with no
# capabilities, no privilege escalation, a read-only root filesystem, and no hostNetwork or hostPID. warn and
# audit stay on restricted, so the exception is reported on every apply.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: monitoring-host
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: privileged
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version: v1.35
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn-version: v1.35
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit-version: v1.35

# L5 (ADR-011): Prometheus on the server node. Service discovery uses Roles only (no ClusterRole): it may
# get, list and watch pods in pg-ha (Patroni and postgres_exporter) and monitoring-host (node_exporter).
# Everything else is a static target reached through its Service.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata: {name: prometheus, namespace: monitoring}
automountServiceAccountToken: true
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata: {name: prometheus-sd, namespace: pg-ha}
rules:
  - {apiGroups: [""], resources: [pods], verbs: [get, list, watch]}
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata: {name: prometheus-sd, namespace: pg-ha}
roleRef: {apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io, kind: Role, name: prometheus-sd}
subjects: [{kind: ServiceAccount, name: prometheus, namespace: monitoring}]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata: {name: prometheus-sd, namespace: monitoring-host}
rules:
  - {apiGroups: [""], resources: [pods], verbs: [get, list, watch]}
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata: {name: prometheus-sd, namespace: monitoring-host}
roleRef: {apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io, kind: Role, name: prometheus-sd}
subjects: [{kind: ServiceAccount, name: prometheus, namespace: monitoring}]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: prometheus, namespace: monitoring}
spec:
  selector: {app.kubernetes.io/name: prometheus}
  ports: [{name: web, port: 9090, targetPort: web}]
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: prometheus, namespace: monitoring}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  strategy: {type: Recreate}      # one TSDB directory, never two writers
  selector: {matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: prometheus}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: prometheus}}
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: prometheus
      enableServiceLinks: false
      nodeSelector: {pg-ha/role: infra}
      tolerations: [{key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, operator: Exists, effect: NoSchedule}]
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 65534
        runAsGroup: 65534
        fsGroup: 65534
        seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}
      containers:
        - name: prometheus
          image: __PROMETHEUS_IMAGE__
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          args:
            - --config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
            - --storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus
            - --storage.tsdb.retention.time=3d
            - --storage.tsdb.retention.size=1GB
            - --web.listen-address=:9090
          ports: [{name: web, containerPort: 9090}]
          readinessProbe: {httpGet: {path: /-/ready, port: web}, periodSeconds: 5}
          livenessProbe: {httpGet: {path: /-/healthy, port: web}, periodSeconds: 15, failureThreshold: 6}
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: 192Mi}
            limits: {memory: 512Mi}
          volumeMounts:
            - {name: config, mountPath: /etc/prometheus, readOnly: true}
            - {name: rules, mountPath: /etc/prometheus/rules, readOnly: true}
            - {name: data, mountPath: /prometheus}
      volumes:
        - name: config
          configMap: {name: prometheus-config}
        - name: rules
          configMap: {name: prometheus-rules}
        # Metrics are for alerting, not history: 3 days at most, lost if the pod moves (docs/observability.md).
        - name: data
          emptyDir: {sizeLimit: 2Gi}

# L5 (ADR-011): Prometheus configuration. Only the pg-ha namespace is scraped for Postgres, so a restored
# cluster in pg-restore is never scraped. The alert rules are scoped to namespace="pg-ha" as well.
global:
  scrape_interval: 10s
  scrape_timeout: 5s
  evaluation_interval: 10s

alerting:
  alertmanagers:
    - static_configs: [{targets: ["alertmanager.monitoring.svc:9093"]}]

rule_files: [/etc/prometheus/rules/*.yml]

scrape_configs:
  # Patroni REST API /metrics on each member (role, timeline, streaming, sync standby).
  - job_name: patroni
    kubernetes_sd_configs:
      - role: pod
        namespaces: {names: [pg-ha]}
        selectors: [{role: pod, label: "app.kubernetes.io/name=pg"}]
    relabel_configs: &member
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_port_name], regex: patroni, action: keep}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_namespace], target_label: namespace}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name], target_label: pod}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name], target_label: node}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name], target_label: instance}

  # postgres_exporter sidecar on each member (pg_stat_archiver, custom pg_ha_* queries).
  - job_name: postgres
    kubernetes_sd_configs:
      - role: pod
        namespaces: {names: [pg-ha]}
        selectors: [{role: pod, label: "app.kubernetes.io/name=pg"}]
    relabel_configs:
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_port_name], regex: metrics, action: keep}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_namespace], target_label: namespace}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name], target_label: pod}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name], target_label: node}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name], target_label: instance}
    metric_relabel_configs:
      - {regex: server, action: labeldrop}     # always 127.0.0.1:5432, adds nothing

  # node_exporter DaemonSet (disk space, memory).
  - job_name: node
    kubernetes_sd_configs:
      - role: pod
        namespaces: {names: [monitoring-host]}
    relabel_configs:
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_port_name], regex: metrics, action: keep}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name], target_label: node}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name], target_label: instance}

  - job_name: kube-state-metrics

    static_configs: [{targets: ["kube-state-metrics.monitoring.svc:8080"]}]

  - job_name: alertmanager
    static_configs: [{targets: ["alertmanager.monitoring.svc:9093"]}]

  - job_name: prometheus
    static_configs: [{targets: ["localhost:9090"]}]

# L5 (ADR-011): node_exporter on every node, for disk space and memory. It is the only workload in the
# monitoring-host namespace, which is the documented Pod Security exception (see namespaces.yaml): a read-only
# hostPath mount of the node's root. No hostNetwork, no hostPID, non-root, no capabilities.
# Each k3d node is a container on the same VM, so every node reports the same host disk.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata: {name: node-exporter, namespace: monitoring-host}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: node-exporter}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: node-exporter}}
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      enableServiceLinks: false
      tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]   # every node, the tainted server included
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 65534
        runAsGroup: 65534
        seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}
      containers:
        - name: node-exporter
          image: __NODE_EXPORTER_IMAGE__
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          args:
            - --path.rootfs=/host
            - --path.procfs=/host/proc
            - --path.sysfs=/host/sys
            - --web.listen-address=:9100
            - --collector.disable-defaults
            - --collector.filesystem
            - --collector.meminfo
            - --collector.loadavg
            - --collector.cpu
            # The node's root is an overlay filesystem (a k3d node is a container), so overlay stays included.
            - --collector.filesystem.fs-types-exclude=^(autofs|binfmt_misc|bpf|cgroup2?|configfs|debugfs|devpts|devtmpfs|fusectl|hugetlbfs|mqueue|nsfs|proc|procfs|pstore|securityfs|sysfs|tracefs|tmpfs|shm)$
            - --collector.filesystem.mount-points-exclude=^/(dev|proc|sys|run|etc|var/lib/kubelet/pods|var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/containerd)($|/)
          ports: [{name: metrics, containerPort: 9100}]
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 10m, memory: 16Mi}
            limits: {memory: 64Mi}
          volumeMounts:
            - {name: root, mountPath: /host, readOnly: true, mountPropagation: HostToContainer}
      volumes:
        - name: root
          hostPath: {path: /}

# L5 (ADR-011). Two namespaces so that only node_exporter runs outside the restricted Pod Security profile.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: monitoring
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version: v1.35
---
# Documented Pod Security exception (R8.7, ADR-011): node_exporter needs a read-only hostPath mount of the
# node's root filesystem to report disk space. hostPath is forbidden by both baseline and restricted, so this
# namespace enforces privileged. It holds node_exporter only. The pod still runs as non-root with no
# capabilities, no privilege escalation, a read-only root filesystem, and no hostNetwork or hostPID. warn and
# audit stay on restricted, so the exception is reported on every apply.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: monitoring-host
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: privileged
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version: v1.35
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn-version: v1.35
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit-version: v1.35

  scrape_timeout: 5s
  evaluation_interval: 10s

alerting:

rule_files: [/etc/prometheus/rules/*.yml]

scrape_configs:
  # Patroni REST API /metrics on each member (role, timeline, streaming, sync standby).
  - job_name: patroni
    kubernetes_sd_configs:
      - role: pod
        namespaces: {names: [pg-ha]}
        selectors: [{role: pod, label: "app.kubernetes.io/name=pg"}]
    relabel_configs: &member

      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name], target_label: node}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name], target_label: instance}

  # postgres_exporter sidecar on each member (pg_stat_archiver, custom pg_ha_* queries).
  - job_name: postgres
    kubernetes_sd_configs:

metadata: {name: alertmanager, namespace: monitoring}

---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: alertmanager, namespace: monitoring}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  strategy: {type: Recreate}
  selector: {matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: alertmanager}}

    metadata: {labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: alertmanager}}

# L5 (ADR-011): node_exporter on every node, for disk space and memory. It is the only workload in the
# monitoring-host namespace, which is the documented Pod Security exception (see namespaces.yaml): a read-only
# hostPath mount of the node's root. No hostNetwork, no hostPID, non-root, no capabilities.
# Each k3d node is a container on the same VM, so every node reports the same host disk.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata: {name: node-exporter, namespace: monitoring-host}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: node-exporter}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: node-exporter}}
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      enableServiceLinks: false
      tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]   # every node, the tainted server included
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 65534
        runAsGroup: 65534
        seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}
      containers:
        - name: node-exporter
          image: __NODE_EXPORTER_IMAGE__
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          args:
            - --path.rootfs=/host
            - --path.procfs=/host/proc
            - --path.sysfs=/host/sys
            - --web.listen-address=:9100
            - --collector.disable-defaults
            - --collector.filesystem
            - --collector.meminfo
            - --collector.loadavg
            - --collector.cpu
            # The node's root is an overlay filesystem (a k3d node is a container), so overlay stays included.
            - --collector.filesystem.fs-types-exclude=^(autofs|binfmt_misc|bpf|cgroup2?|configfs|debugfs|devpts|devtmpfs|fusectl|hugetlbfs|mqueue|nsfs|proc|procfs|pstore|securityfs|sysfs|tracefs|tmpfs|shm)$
            - --collector.filesystem.mount-points-exclude=^/(dev|proc|sys|run|etc|var/lib/kubelet/pods|var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/containerd)($|/)
          ports: [{name: metrics, containerPort: 9100}]
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 10m, memory: 16Mi}
            limits: {memory: 64Mi}
          volumeMounts:
            - {name: root, mountPath: /host, readOnly: true, mountPropagation: HostToContainer}
      volumes:
        - name: root
          hostPath: {path: /}

# L5 (ADR-011, R10.2): alert rules. Every Postgres, backup and restore rule is scoped to namespace="pg-ha", so
# a restored cluster in pg-restore never pages (it is not scraped either). Each rule has a severity, a summary
# and a "why" annotation that explains its threshold. Unit tests: tests/alerts/pg-ha.test.yml (make test-alerts).
# Severities: critical = data or availability at risk now; warning = degraded or needs attention today;
# info = a record that something happened. Full table: docs/observability.md.
groups:
  - name: pg-ha-replication
    rules:
      - alert: NoPrimary
        expr: |
          sum by (namespace) (patroni_primary{namespace="pg-ha"}) < 1
          or absent(patroni_primary{namespace="pg-ha"})
        for: 45s
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "No Patroni member is primary in {{ $labels.namespace }}; writes are failing."
          why: "Automatic failover is measured at 26 s at worst (L2 node mode, target 30 s). 45 s means failover itself has not completed."

      - alert: MultiplePrimaries
        expr: |
          sum by (namespace) (patroni_primary{namespace="pg-ha"}) > 1
          or count by (namespace) (pg_replication_is_replica{namespace="pg-ha"} == 0) > 1
        for: 20s
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "More than one member reports itself primary in {{ $labels.namespace }} (split brain)."
          why: "Members are scraped at slightly different moments, so one scrape can show the old and new primary during a switchover. Two consecutive evaluations (20 s) rule that out."

      - alert: MemberDown
        expr: |
          up{namespace="pg-ha", job="patroni"} == 0
          or patroni_postgres_running{namespace="pg-ha"} == 0
          or count by (namespace) (up{namespace="pg-ha", job="patroni"} == 1)
             < on (namespace) kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace="pg-ha", statefulset="pg"}
        for: 30s
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Patroni member {{ $labels.pod }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} is down or Postgres is not running (a missing pod has no pod label)."
          why: "A pod restart takes 10-20 s and Patroni's leader ttl is 20 s. 30 s filters a normal restart. Warning, because the cluster still serves with two members."

      - alert: ReplicaNotStreaming
        expr: |
          count by (namespace) (patroni_postgres_streaming{namespace="pg-ha"} == 1)
            < on (namespace) (kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace="pg-ha", statefulset="pg"} - 1)
          or max by (namespace) (
            kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace="pg-ha", statefulset="pg"} > 1
            unless on (namespace) patroni_postgres_streaming{namespace="pg-ha"} == 1)
        for: 2m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Fewer standbys are streaming than expected in {{ $labels.namespace }} (a member is down, re-cloning or disconnected)."
          why: "A diverged member is re-cloned (ADR-008), about 1 min at this data size (L4). 2 min avoids paging on a normal rejoin. Raise it as the database grows."

      - alert: ReplicationLagHigh
        expr: max by (namespace, application_name) (pg_ha_replication_lag_bytes{namespace="pg-ha"}) > 16 * 1024 * 1024
        for: 2m
        labels: {severity: warning, lag: bytes}
        annotations:
          summary: "Standby {{ $labels.application_name }} is {{ $value | humanize1024 }}B behind the primary's WAL in {{ $labels.namespace }}."
          why: "Above maximum_lag_on_failover (1 MiB) Patroni will not promote that standby. 16 MiB (one WAL segment) for 2 min filters bulk loads such as make seed."

      - alert: ReplicationLagHigh
        expr: max by (namespace, application_name) (pg_ha_replication_replay_lag_seconds{namespace="pg-ha"}) > 30
        for: 2m
        labels: {severity: warning, lag: seconds}
        annotations:
          summary: "Standby {{ $labels.application_name }} replays {{ $value | humanizeDuration }} behind the primary in {{ $labels.namespace }}."
          why: "30 s equals the RTO target: a promoted standby that far behind would add that much replay time. 2 min filters bursts."

      - alert: SyncStandbyMissing
        expr: |
          sum by (namespace) (patroni_sync_standby{namespace="pg-ha"}) < 1
          and on (namespace) sum by (namespace) (patroni_primary{namespace="pg-ha"}) == 1
        for: 1m
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "The primary in {{ $labels.namespace }} has no synchronous standby; commits are not replicated before they are acknowledged."
          why: "synchronous_mode is non-strict (ADR-004), so the primary keeps writing without a standby, and Patroni will not fail over automatically. Patroni picks a new sync standby within a few 3 s loops, so 1 min means none is eligible."

      - alert: SlotWALRetentionHigh
        expr: max by (namespace, pod, slot_name) (pg_ha_slot_retained_bytes{namespace="pg-ha"}) > 512 * 1024 * 1024
        for: 5m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Slot {{ $labels.slot_name }} on {{ $labels.pod }} holds {{ $value | humanize1024 }}B of WAL."
          why: "Half of max_slot_wal_keep_size (1 GB, ADR-005). Leaves time to act before Postgres invalidates the slot and the standby must use the archive or a re-clone."

      - alert: SlotLost
        expr: max by (namespace, pod, slot_name) (pg_ha_slot_lost{namespace="pg-ha"}) == 1
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Slot {{ $labels.slot_name }} on {{ $labels.pod }} was invalidated (wal_status lost)."
          why: "Any lost slot means the 1 GB cap was reached. The standby now depends on restore_command from the archive or on a re-clone."

      - alert: FailoverOccurred
        expr: |
          max by (namespace) (patroni_postgres_timeline{namespace="pg-ha"})
            > max by (namespace) (patroni_postgres_timeline{namespace="pg-ha"} offset 5m)
        labels: {severity: info}
        annotations:
          summary: "The timeline in {{ $labels.namespace }} increased in the last 5 min: a member was promoted (failover or switchover)."
          why: "Informational. Every promotion starts a new timeline. It clears 5 min later."

  - name: pg-ha-archive-backup
    rules:
      - alert: ArchiveFailing
        expr: increase(pg_stat_archiver_failed_count{namespace="pg-ha"}[5m]) > 0
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "WAL archiving on {{ $labels.pod }} failed in the last 5 min."
          why: "Any failure means WAL is not reaching the repository. A single failure during a Garage restart warns and clears within 5 min. ArchiveStale is the page."

      - alert: ArchiveStale
        expr: max by (namespace, pod) (pg_ha_archive_oldest_ready_seconds{namespace="pg-ha"}) > 120
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "A completed WAL segment on {{ $labels.pod }} has waited {{ $value | humanizeDuration }} to be archived; PITR is losing data."
          why: "A segment is closed at most archive_timeout (60 s) after its first write, and a Garage restart delays archiving by about 60 s (L3). 120 s on top of that means writes from more than 3 min ago are not in the repository. An idle cluster closes no segment, so it does not fire."

      - alert: BackupFailed
        expr: |
          (
            max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_failed{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+", condition="true"} == 1)
            > max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"} > 0)
          )
          or (
            max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_failed{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+", condition="true"} == 1)
            unless on (namespace) max by (namespace) (kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"} > 0)
          )
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "The most recent backup Job in {{ $labels.namespace }} failed."
          why: "The backup Job exits non-zero on any backup, expire or verify error, so a failed Job means the newest backup is missing or unverified. It clears when a newer backup Job succeeds."

      - alert: BackupStale
        expr: |
          time() - max by (namespace) (
            kube_job_status_completion_time{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"} > 0
            or kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-backup"}
          ) > 26 * 3600
          or (
            time() - max by (namespace) (kube_cronjob_created{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-backup"}) > 26 * 3600
            unless on (namespace) max by (namespace) (
              kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"} > 0
              or kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-backup"})
          )
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "No backup in {{ $labels.namespace }} has succeeded for more than 26 h."
          why: "The backup runs daily at 20:00 UTC (ADR-009). 26 h allows a run that is late or slow but not a missed day. A new cluster gets 26 h from the CronJob's creation."

      - alert: RestoreTestFailed
        expr: |
          (
            max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_failed{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*", condition="true"} == 1)
            > max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"} > 0)
          )
          or (
            max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_failed{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*", condition="true"} == 1)
            unless on (namespace) max by (namespace) (kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"} > 0)
          )
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "The most recent restore-test Job in {{ $labels.namespace }} failed; the newest backup may not be restorable."
          why: "The restore test exits non-zero on any restore, recovery or pg_amcheck error (ADR-010). It clears when a newer restore test succeeds."

      - alert: RestoreTestStale
        expr: |
          time() - max by (namespace) (
            kube_job_status_completion_time{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"} > 0
            or kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-restore-test"}
          ) > 26 * 3600
          or (
            time() - max by (namespace) (kube_cronjob_created{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-restore-test"}) > 26 * 3600
            unless on (namespace) max by (namespace) (
              kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"} > 0
              or kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-restore-test"})
          )
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "No restore test in {{ $labels.namespace }} has succeeded for more than 26 h."
          why: "The restore test runs daily at 21:00 UTC (ADR-010). 26 h allows a late run but not a missed day."

  - name: pg-ha-platform
    rules:
      - alert: DiskLow
        expr: |
          node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint="/"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{mountpoint="/"} < 0.15
        for: 5m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Node {{ $labels.node }} has {{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of its root filesystem free."
          why: "local-path volumes are not size-limited, so data, WAL, the restore test's emptyDir (up to 4 Gi) and the 1 GB slot cap all share this disk. 15% of the 48 GB host is about 7 GB, which still fits a restore test and a full slot."

      - alert: CoreDNSNotReady
        expr: kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="kube-system", deployment="coredns"} < 1
        for: 1m
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "CoreDNS has no available replica; promotion and archiving cannot resolve Garage."
          why: "Promotion runs restore_command, which resolves Garage through cluster DNS (L3). A CoreDNS restart takes 10-20 s, so 1 min is a real outage."

      - alert: MonitoringTargetDown
        expr: up{job=~"kube-state-metrics|node|alertmanager"} == 0
        for: 5m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Scrape target {{ $labels.job }}/{{ $labels.instance }} is down; alerts that depend on it are blind."
          why: "Backup, restore-test, CoreDNS and disk alerts read these targets and stay silent without them. 5 min tolerates a restart or a stopped node during a failover test."

          or count by (namespace) (up{namespace="pg-ha", job="patroni"} == 1)
             < on (namespace) kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace="pg-ha", statefulset="pg"}
        for: 30s
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Patroni member {{ $labels.pod }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} is down or Postgres is not running (a missing pod has no pod label)."
          why: "A pod restart takes 10-20 s and Patroni's leader ttl is 20 s. 30 s filters a normal restart. Warning, because the cluster still serves with two members."

      - alert: ReplicaNotStreaming

          count by (namespace) (patroni_postgres_streaming{namespace="pg-ha"} == 1)
            < on (namespace) (kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace="pg-ha", statefulset="pg"} - 1)
          or max by (namespace) (
            kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace="pg-ha", statefulset="pg"} > 1
            unless on (namespace) patroni_postgres_streaming{namespace="pg-ha"} == 1)
        for: 2m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Fewer standbys are streaming than expected in {{ $labels.namespace }} (a member is down, re-cloning or disconnected)."
          why: "A diverged member is re-cloned (ADR-008), about 1 min at this data size (L4). 2 min avoids paging on a normal rejoin. Raise it as the database grows."

      - alert: ReplicationLagHigh
        expr: max by (namespace, application_name) (pg_ha_replication_lag_bytes{namespace="pg-ha"}) > 16 * 1024 * 1024
        for: 2m
        labels: {severity: warning, lag: bytes}
        annotations:
          summary: "Standby {{ $labels.application_name }} is {{ $value | humanize1024 }}B behind the primary's WAL in {{ $labels.namespace }}."
          why: "Above maximum_lag_on_failover (1 MiB) Patroni will not promote that standby. 16 MiB (one WAL segment) for 2 min filters bulk loads such as make seed."

      - alert: ReplicationLagHigh
        expr: max by (namespace, application_name) (pg_ha_replication_replay_lag_seconds{namespace="pg-ha"}) > 30
        for: 2m
        labels: {severity: warning, lag: seconds}
        annotations:
          summary: "Standby {{ $labels.application_name }} replays {{ $value | humanizeDuration }} behind the primary in {{ $labels.namespace }}."
          why: "30 s equals the RTO target: a promoted standby that far behind would add that much replay time. 2 min filters bursts."

      - alert: SyncStandbyMissing
        expr: |
          sum by (namespace) (patroni_sync_standby{namespace="pg-ha"}) < 1
          and on (namespace) sum by (namespace) (patroni_primary{namespace="pg-ha"}) == 1
        for: 1m
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "The primary in {{ $labels.namespace }} has no synchronous standby; commits are not replicated before they are acknowledged."
          why: "synchronous_mode is non-strict (ADR-004), so the primary keeps writing without a standby, and Patroni will not fail over automatically. Patroni picks a new sync standby within a few 3 s loops, so 1 min means none is eligible."

      - alert: SlotWALRetentionHigh
        expr: max by (namespace, pod, slot_name) (pg_ha_slot_retained_bytes{namespace="pg-ha"}) > 512 * 1024 * 1024
        for: 5m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Slot {{ $labels.slot_name }} on {{ $labels.pod }} holds {{ $value | humanize1024 }}B of WAL."
          why: "Half of max_slot_wal_keep_size (1 GB, ADR-005). Leaves time to act before Postgres invalidates the slot and the standby must use the archive or a re-clone."

      - alert: SlotLost
        expr: max by (namespace, pod, slot_name) (pg_ha_slot_lost{namespace="pg-ha"}) == 1
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Slot {{ $labels.slot_name }} on {{ $labels.pod }} was invalidated (wal_status lost)."
          why: "Any lost slot means the 1 GB cap was reached. The standby now depends on restore_command from the archive or on a re-clone."

      - alert: FailoverOccurred
        expr: |
          max by (namespace) (patroni_postgres_timeline{namespace="pg-ha"})
            > max by (namespace) (patroni_postgres_timeline{namespace="pg-ha"} offset 5m)
        labels: {severity: info}
        annotations:
          summary: "The timeline in {{ $labels.namespace }} increased in the last 5 min: a member was promoted (failover or switchover)."
          why: "Informational. Every promotion starts a new timeline. It clears 5 min later."

        expr: increase(pg_stat_archiver_failed_count{namespace="pg-ha"}[5m]) > 0
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "WAL archiving on {{ $labels.pod }} failed in the last 5 min."
          why: "Any failure means WAL is not reaching the repository. A single failure during a Garage restart warns and clears within 5 min. ArchiveStale is the page."

      - alert: ArchiveStale
        expr: max by (namespace, pod) (pg_ha_archive_oldest_ready_seconds{namespace="pg-ha"}) > 120
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "A completed WAL segment on {{ $labels.pod }} has waited {{ $value | humanizeDuration }} to be archived; PITR is losing data."

              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_failed{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+", condition="true"} == 1)

        annotations:

            or kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-backup"}
          ) > 26 * 3600
          or (
            time() - max by (namespace) (kube_cronjob_created{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-backup"}) > 26 * 3600
            unless on (namespace) max by (namespace) (
              kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"} > 0
              or kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-backup"})
          )
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "No backup in {{ $labels.namespace }} has succeeded for more than 26 h."
          why: "The backup runs daily at 20:00 UTC (ADR-009). 26 h allows a run that is late or slow but not a missed day. A new cluster gets 26 h from the CronJob's creation."

      - alert: RestoreTestFailed
        expr: |
          (
            max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_failed{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*", condition="true"} == 1)
            > max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"} > 0)
          )
          or (
            max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_failed{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*", condition="true"} == 1)
            unless on (namespace) max by (namespace) (kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"} > 0)
          )
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "The most recent restore-test Job in {{ $labels.namespace }} failed; the newest backup may not be restorable."
          why: "The restore test exits non-zero on any restore, recovery or pg_amcheck error (ADR-010). It clears when a newer restore test succeeds."

      - alert: RestoreTestStale
        expr: |
          time() - max by (namespace) (
            kube_job_status_completion_time{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"} > 0
            or kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-restore-test"}
          ) > 26 * 3600
          or (
            time() - max by (namespace) (kube_cronjob_created{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-restore-test"}) > 26 * 3600
            unless on (namespace) max by (namespace) (
              kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"} > 0
              or kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-restore-test"})
          )
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "No restore test in {{ $labels.namespace }} has succeeded for more than 26 h."
          why: "The restore test runs daily at 21:00 UTC (ADR-010). 26 h allows a late run but not a missed day."

  - name: pg-ha-platform
    rules:
      - alert: DiskLow
        expr: |
          node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint="/"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{mountpoint="/"} < 0.15
        for: 5m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Node {{ $labels.node }} has {{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of its root filesystem free."
          why: "local-path volumes are not size-limited, so data, WAL, the restore test's emptyDir (up to 4 Gi) and the 1 GB slot cap all share this disk. 15% of the 48 GB host is about 7 GB, which still fits a restore test and a full slot."

      - alert: CoreDNSNotReady
        expr: kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="kube-system", deployment="coredns"} < 1
        for: 1m
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "CoreDNS has no available replica; promotion and archiving cannot resolve Garage."
          why: "Promotion runs restore_command, which resolves Garage through cluster DNS (L3). A CoreDNS restart takes 10-20 s, so 1 min is a real outage."

      - alert: MonitoringTargetDown
        expr: up{job=~"kube-state-metrics|node|alertmanager"} == 0
        for: 5m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Scrape target {{ $labels.job }}/{{ $labels.instance }} is down; alerts that depend on it are blind."
          why: "Backup, restore-test, CoreDNS and disk alerts read these targets and stay silent without them. 5 min tolerates a restart or a stopped node during a failover test."

# L5 (ADR-011): Prometheus configuration. Only the pg-ha namespace is scraped for Postgres, so a restored
# cluster in pg-restore is never scraped. The alert rules are scoped to namespace="pg-ha" as well.
global:
  scrape_interval: 10s
  scrape_timeout: 5s
  evaluation_interval: 10s

alerting:
  alertmanagers:
    - static_configs: [{targets: ["alertmanager.monitoring.svc:9093"]}]

rule_files: [/etc/prometheus/rules/*.yml]

scrape_configs:
  # Patroni REST API /metrics on each member (role, timeline, streaming, sync standby).
  - job_name: patroni
    kubernetes_sd_configs:
      - role: pod
        namespaces: {names: [pg-ha]}
        selectors: [{role: pod, label: "app.kubernetes.io/name=pg"}]
    relabel_configs: &member
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_port_name], regex: patroni, action: keep}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_namespace], target_label: namespace}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name], target_label: pod}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name], target_label: node}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name], target_label: instance}

  # postgres_exporter sidecar on each member (pg_stat_archiver, custom pg_ha_* queries).
  - job_name: postgres
    kubernetes_sd_configs:
      - role: pod
        namespaces: {names: [pg-ha]}
        selectors: [{role: pod, label: "app.kubernetes.io/name=pg"}]
    relabel_configs:
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_port_name], regex: metrics, action: keep}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_namespace], target_label: namespace}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name], target_label: pod}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name], target_label: node}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name], target_label: instance}
    metric_relabel_configs:
      - {regex: server, action: labeldrop}     # always 127.0.0.1:5432, adds nothing

  # node_exporter DaemonSet (disk space, memory).
  - job_name: node
    kubernetes_sd_configs:
      - role: pod
        namespaces: {names: [monitoring-host]}
    relabel_configs:
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_port_name], regex: metrics, action: keep}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name], target_label: node}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name], target_label: instance}

  # kube-state-metrics: Job, CronJob, StatefulSet and Deployment state in pg-ha and kube-system.
  # honor_labels keeps the object's own namespace label.
  - job_name: kube-state-metrics
    honor_labels: true
    static_configs: [{targets: ["kube-state-metrics.monitoring.svc:8080"]}]

  - job_name: alertmanager
    static_configs: [{targets: ["alertmanager.monitoring.svc:9093"]}]

  - job_name: prometheus
    static_configs: [{targets: ["localhost:9090"]}]

        annotations:
          summary: "No restore test in {{ $labels.namespace }} has succeeded for more than 26 h."
          why: "The restore test runs daily at 21:00 UTC (ADR-010). 26 h allows a late run but not a missed day."

          summary: "Node {{ $labels.node }} has {{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of its root filesystem free."
          why: "local-path volumes are not size-limited, so data, WAL, the restore test's emptyDir (up to 4 Gi) and the 1 GB slot cap all share this disk. 15% of the 48 GB host is about 7 GB, which still fits a restore test and a full slot."
