# L5 (ADR-011, R10.2): alert rules. Every Postgres, backup and restore rule is scoped to namespace="pg-ha", so
# a restored cluster in pg-restore never pages (it is not scraped either). Each rule has a severity, a summary
# and a "why" annotation that explains its threshold. Unit tests: tests/alerts/pg-ha.test.yml (make test-alerts).
# Severities: critical = data or availability at risk now; warning = degraded or needs attention today;
# info = a record that something happened. Full table: docs/observability.md.
groups:
  - name: pg-ha-replication
    rules:
      - alert: NoPrimary
        expr: |
          sum by (namespace) (patroni_primary{namespace="pg-ha"}) < 1
          or absent(patroni_primary{namespace="pg-ha"})
        for: 45s
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "No Patroni member is primary in {{ $labels.namespace }}; writes are failing."
          why: "Automatic failover is measured at 26 s at worst (L2 node mode, target 30 s). 45 s means failover itself has not completed."

      - alert: MultiplePrimaries
        expr: |
          sum by (namespace) (patroni_primary{namespace="pg-ha"}) > 1
          or count by (namespace) (pg_replication_is_replica{namespace="pg-ha"} == 0) > 1
        for: 20s
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "More than one member reports itself primary in {{ $labels.namespace }} (split brain)."
          why: "Members are scraped at slightly different moments, so one scrape can show the old and new primary during a switchover. Two consecutive evaluations (20 s) rule that out."

      - alert: MemberDown
        expr: |
          up{namespace="pg-ha", job="patroni"} == 0
          or patroni_postgres_running{namespace="pg-ha"} == 0
          or count by (namespace) (up{namespace="pg-ha", job="patroni"} == 1)
             < on (namespace) kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace="pg-ha", statefulset="pg"}
        for: 30s
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Patroni member {{ $labels.pod }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} is down or Postgres is not running (a missing pod has no pod label)."
          why: "A pod restart takes 10-20 s and Patroni's leader ttl is 20 s. 30 s filters a normal restart. Warning, because the cluster still serves with two members."

      - alert: ReplicaNotStreaming
        expr: |
          count by (namespace) (patroni_postgres_streaming{namespace="pg-ha"} == 1)
            < on (namespace) (kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace="pg-ha", statefulset="pg"} - 1)
          or max by (namespace) (
            kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace="pg-ha", statefulset="pg"} > 1
            unless on (namespace) patroni_postgres_streaming{namespace="pg-ha"} == 1)
        for: 2m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Fewer standbys are streaming than expected in {{ $labels.namespace }} (a member is down, re-cloning or disconnected)."
          why: "A diverged member is re-cloned (ADR-008), about 1 min at this data size (L4). 2 min avoids paging on a normal rejoin. Raise it as the database grows."

      - alert: ReplicationLagHigh
        expr: max by (namespace, application_name) (pg_ha_replication_lag_bytes{namespace="pg-ha"}) > 16 * 1024 * 1024
        for: 2m
        labels: {severity: warning, lag: bytes}
        annotations:
          summary: "Standby {{ $labels.application_name }} is {{ $value | humanize1024 }}B behind the primary's WAL in {{ $labels.namespace }}."
          why: "Above maximum_lag_on_failover (1 MiB) Patroni will not promote that standby. 16 MiB (one WAL segment) for 2 min filters bulk loads such as make seed."

      - alert: ReplicationLagHigh
        expr: max by (namespace, application_name) (pg_ha_replication_replay_lag_seconds{namespace="pg-ha"}) > 30
        for: 2m
        labels: {severity: warning, lag: seconds}
        annotations:
          summary: "Standby {{ $labels.application_name }} replays {{ $value | humanizeDuration }} behind the primary in {{ $labels.namespace }}."
          why: "30 s equals the RTO target: a promoted standby that far behind would add that much replay time. 2 min filters bursts."

      - alert: SyncStandbyMissing
        expr: |
          sum by (namespace) (patroni_sync_standby{namespace="pg-ha"}) < 1
          and on (namespace) sum by (namespace) (patroni_primary{namespace="pg-ha"}) == 1
        for: 1m
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "The primary in {{ $labels.namespace }} has no synchronous standby; commits are not replicated before they are acknowledged."
          why: "synchronous_mode is non-strict (ADR-004), so the primary keeps writing without a standby, and Patroni will not fail over automatically. Patroni picks a new sync standby within a few 3 s loops, so 1 min means none is eligible."

      - alert: SlotWALRetentionHigh
        expr: max by (namespace, pod, slot_name) (pg_ha_slot_retained_bytes{namespace="pg-ha"}) > 512 * 1024 * 1024
        for: 5m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Slot {{ $labels.slot_name }} on {{ $labels.pod }} holds {{ $value | humanize1024 }}B of WAL."
          why: "Half of max_slot_wal_keep_size (1 GB, ADR-005). Leaves time to act before Postgres invalidates the slot and the standby must use the archive or a re-clone."

      - alert: SlotLost
        expr: max by (namespace, pod, slot_name) (pg_ha_slot_lost{namespace="pg-ha"}) == 1
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Slot {{ $labels.slot_name }} on {{ $labels.pod }} was invalidated (wal_status lost)."
          why: "Any lost slot means the 1 GB cap was reached. The standby now depends on restore_command from the archive or on a re-clone."

      - alert: FailoverOccurred
        expr: |
          max by (namespace) (patroni_postgres_timeline{namespace="pg-ha"})
            > max by (namespace) (patroni_postgres_timeline{namespace="pg-ha"} offset 5m)
        labels: {severity: info}
        annotations:
          summary: "The timeline in {{ $labels.namespace }} increased in the last 5 min: a member was promoted (failover or switchover)."
          why: "Informational. Every promotion starts a new timeline. It clears 5 min later."

  - name: pg-ha-archive-backup
    rules:
      - alert: ArchiveFailing
        expr: increase(pg_stat_archiver_failed_count{namespace="pg-ha"}[5m]) > 0
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "WAL archiving on {{ $labels.pod }} failed in the last 5 min."
          why: "Any failure means WAL is not reaching the repository. A single failure during a Garage restart warns and clears within 5 min. ArchiveStale is the page."

      - alert: ArchiveStale
        expr: max by (namespace, pod) (pg_ha_archive_oldest_ready_seconds{namespace="pg-ha"}) > 120
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "A completed WAL segment on {{ $labels.pod }} has waited {{ $value | humanizeDuration }} to be archived; PITR is losing data."
          why: "A segment is closed at most archive_timeout (60 s) after its first write, and a Garage restart delays archiving by about 60 s (L3). 120 s on top of that means writes from more than 3 min ago are not in the repository. An idle cluster closes no segment, so it does not fire."

      - alert: BackupFailed
        expr: |
          (
            max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_failed{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+", condition="true"} == 1)
            > max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"} > 0)
          )
          or (
            max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_failed{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+", condition="true"} == 1)
            unless on (namespace) max by (namespace) (kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"} > 0)
          )
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "The most recent backup Job in {{ $labels.namespace }} failed."
          why: "The backup Job exits non-zero on any backup, expire or verify error, so a failed Job means the newest backup is missing or unverified. It clears when a newer backup Job succeeds."

      - alert: BackupStale
        expr: |
          time() - max by (namespace) (
            kube_job_status_completion_time{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"} > 0
            or kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-backup"}
          ) > 26 * 3600
          or (
            time() - max by (namespace) (kube_cronjob_created{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-backup"}) > 26 * 3600
            unless on (namespace) max by (namespace) (
              kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+"} > 0
              or kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-backup"})
          )
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "No backup in {{ $labels.namespace }} has succeeded for more than 26 h."
          why: "The backup runs daily at 20:00 UTC (ADR-009). 26 h allows a run that is late or slow but not a missed day. A new cluster gets 26 h from the CronJob's creation."

      - alert: RestoreTestFailed
        expr: |
          (
            max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_failed{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*", condition="true"} == 1)
            > max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"} > 0)
          )
          or (
            max by (namespace) (kube_job_created{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_failed{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*", condition="true"} == 1)
            unless on (namespace) max by (namespace) (kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"} > 0)
          )
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "The most recent restore-test Job in {{ $labels.namespace }} failed; the newest backup may not be restorable."
          why: "The restore test exits non-zero on any restore, recovery or pg_amcheck error (ADR-010). It clears when a newer restore test succeeds."

      - alert: RestoreTestStale
        expr: |
          time() - max by (namespace) (
            kube_job_status_completion_time{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"}
              and on (namespace, job_name) kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"} > 0
            or kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-restore-test"}
          ) > 26 * 3600
          or (
            time() - max by (namespace) (kube_cronjob_created{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-restore-test"}) > 26 * 3600
            unless on (namespace) max by (namespace) (
              kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-restore-test.*"} > 0
              or kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{namespace="pg-ha", cronjob="pg-restore-test"})
          )
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "No restore test in {{ $labels.namespace }} has succeeded for more than 26 h."
          why: "The restore test runs daily at 21:00 UTC (ADR-010). 26 h allows a late run but not a missed day."

  - name: pg-ha-platform
    rules:
      - alert: DiskLow
        expr: |
          node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint="/"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{mountpoint="/"} < 0.15
        for: 5m

      - alert: CoreDNSNotReady
        expr: kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="kube-system", deployment="coredns"} < 1
        for: 1m
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "CoreDNS has no available replica; promotion and archiving cannot resolve Garage."
          why: "Promotion runs restore_command, which resolves Garage through cluster DNS (L3). A CoreDNS restart takes 10-20 s, so 1 min is a real outage."

      - alert: MonitoringTargetDown

        for: 5m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L5 (ADR-011): deploys Prometheus, Alertmanager, kube-state-metrics and node_exporter from deploy/monitoring
# with the pinned images, then waits until every scrape target is up. Idempotent. Part of make up.
# The postgres_exporter sidecar is part of the StatefulSet (scripts/deploy.sh), so it is not applied here.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
cluster_exists || die "cluster $CLUSTER_NAME not found, run: make cluster"
kubectl get ns "$PG_NS" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "namespace $PG_NS not found, run: make deploy"

kubectl kustomize "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/monitoring" |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L5: lists the alerts Alertmanager currently holds, read through the API server's service proxy (no exec,
# no port-forward). ALL=1 also lists Prometheus's pending alerts (condition true, 'for' not yet elapsed).
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
P=/api/v1/namespaces/monitoring/services
am=$(kubectl get --raw "$P/alertmanager:9093/proxy/api/v2/alerts?active=true&silenced=false&inhibited=false") ||
  die "Alertmanager not reachable, run: make monitoring"
printf 'Firing alerts in Alertmanager at %s (UTC):\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
n=$(jq length <<<"$am")
if [ "$n" = 0 ]; then echo "  none"
else jq -r 'sort_by(.labels.severity, .labels.alertname)[] |
  "  \(.labels.severity | ascii_upcase | .[0:4])  \(.labels.alertname)\(if .labels.lag then "/" + .labels.lag else "" end)  since \(.startsAt[0:19])Z  \(.annotations.summary)"' <<<"$am"; fi
if [ "${ALL:-0}" = 1 ]; then
  printf '\nPending in Prometheus:\n'
  kubectl get --raw "$P/prometheus:9090/proxy/api/v1/alerts" |
    jq -r '[.data.alerts[] | select(.state == "pending")] | if length == 0 then "  none" else .[] | "  \(.labels.alertname)  since \(.activeAt[0:19])Z" end'
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the L5 monitoring tests. Each test writes docs/evidence/L5/<part>.md, then regenerates
# docs/evidence/L5-monitoring.md. Prometheus and Alertmanager are read through the API server's service proxy,
# so no port-forward or exec is needed. SQL runs in the test client pod (tests/lib.sh, D4).
. "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/lib.sh"
mkdir -p "$EV_DIR/L5"
SVC=/api/v1/namespaces/monitoring/services
uri() { jq -rn --arg q "$1" '$q|@uri'; }
# promq QUERY: instant query, one line per series: {labels} value
promq() { kubectl get --raw "$SVC/prometheus:9090/proxy/api/v1/query?query=$(uri "$1")" |
  jq -r '.data.result[] | "\(.metric | del(.__name__) | to_entries | map("\(.key)=\(.value)") | join(",")) \(.value[1])"'; }
# promv QUERY: the single value of a scalar-like query, or empty
promv() { kubectl get --raw "$SVC/prometheus:9090/proxy/api/v1/query?query=$(uri "$1")" | jq -r '.data.result[0].value[1] // empty'; }
# Alertmanager's active alerts as JSON, and one line per alert for the evidence.
am_json() { kubectl get --raw "$SVC/alertmanager:9093/proxy/api/v2/alerts?active=true&silenced=false&inhibited=false"; }
am_lines() { am_json | jq -r 'sort_by(.labels.alertname)[] | "\(.labels.alertname)\(if .labels.lag then "/" + .labels.lag else "" end) severity=\(.labels.severity) pod=\(.labels.pod // "-") startsAt=\(.startsAt)"'; }
am_has() { am_json | jq -e --arg a "$1" 'any(.[]; .labels.alertname == $a and .labels.namespace != "pg-restore")' >/dev/null; }

# wait_alerts STATE TIMEOUT ALERT...: polls Alertmanager every 5 s until every ALERT is firing (STATE=firing) or
# none is (STATE=resolved). Records first-seen and gone times in SEEN_<name> and GONE_<name> (epoch seconds).
wait_alerts() {
  local state=$1 end=$((SECONDS + $2)) a ok cur; shift 2
  while :; do
    cur=$(am_json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[] | select(.labels.namespace != "pg-restore") | .labels.alertname' | sort -u) || cur=
    ok=1
    for a in "$@"; do
      if grep -qx "$a" <<<"$cur"; then [ -n "$(eval echo "\${SEEN_$a:-}")" ] || eval "SEEN_$a=$(date +%s)"
        [ "$state" = firing ] || ok=0
      else [ -z "$(eval echo "\${SEEN_$a:-}")" ] || [ -n "$(eval echo "\${GONE_$a:-}")" ] || eval "GONE_$a=$(date +%s)"
        [ "$state" = resolved ] || ok=0
      fi
    done
    [ $ok = 1 ] && return 0
    [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || return 1
    sleep 5
  done
}
# ts EPOCH: UTC clock time, or n/a
ts() { [ -n "${1:-}" ] && date -u -d "@$1" +%H:%M:%S || echo n/a; }
# Seconds between two epochs, or n/a
dt() { [ -n "${1:-}" ] && [ -n "${2:-}" ] && echo $(( $2 - $1 )) || echo n/a; }

l5_finish() { # part title description make-target
  local verdict=PASS; [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ] || verdict=FAIL
  { printf '# L5: %s\n\n**Result: %s**\n\n' "$2" "$verdict"
    printf -- '- **What:** %s\n' "$3"
    printf -- '- **Run:** %s (UTC), %s s\n- **Reproduce:** `make %s`\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))" "$4"
    printf -- '- **Versions:** Prometheus `%s`, Alertmanager `%s`, postgres_exporter `%s`, image `%s`\n' "${PROMETHEUS_IMAGE%%@*}" "${ALERTMANAGER_IMAGE%%@*}" "${POSTGRES_EXPORTER_IMAGE%%@*}" "$PG_IMAGE"
    [ ! -f "$EV_DIR/L5-monitoring-history.md" ] || printf -- '- **History:** [`L5-monitoring-history.md`](../L5-monitoring-history.md) (maintained by hand)\n'
    printf '\n## Checks\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n'; cat "$CHECKS"; cat "$BODY"; } | redact > "$EV_DIR/L5/$1.md"
  "$ROOT_DIR/tests/l5-summary.sh"
  log "RESULT L5 $1: $verdict -> docs/evidence/L5/$1.md"
  rm -f "$BODY" "$CHECKS"
  [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]
}

. "$(dirname "$0")/../scripts/spikes/lib.sh"
PARTS="alert-rules:Alert rule unit tests (R10.2)
metrics:Scrape targets, key series, lag measurement and resources (R10.1, R1.7)
alerts-failover:Alerts on a node failover (R10.3)
alerts-archive:Alerts on an object-storage outage (R10.3, R9.6)"
{ printf '# L5: monitoring and alerting\n\nGenerated from the per-part files in [`L5/`](L5/) each time a part runs. Timestamps are UTC. Design and alert table: [`../observability.md`](../observability.md).\n\n'
  [ ! -f "$EV_DIR/L5-monitoring-history.md" ] || printf 'Hand-written notes: [`L5-monitoring-history.md`](L5-monitoring-history.md).\n\n'
  printf '| Part | Result | Checks passed | Details |\n|---|---|---:|---|\n'
  while IFS=: read -r f t; do
    if [ -f "$EV_DIR/L5/$f.md" ]; then
      r=$(grep -m1 -oE 'Result: (PASS|FAIL)' "$EV_DIR/L5/$f.md" | cut -d' ' -f2)
      p=$(grep -c '| PASS |$' "$EV_DIR/L5/$f.md" || true); n=$(grep -cE '\| (PASS|\*\*FAIL\*\*) \|$' "$EV_DIR/L5/$f.md" || true)
      printf '| %s | %s | %s of %s | [`L5/%s.md`](L5/%s.md) |\n' "$t" "$r" "$p" "$n" "$f" "$f"

  done <<<"$PARTS"; } > "$EV_DIR/L5-monitoring.md"

am_lines() { am_json | jq -r 'sort_by(.labels.alertname)[] | "\(.labels.alertname)\(if .labels.lag then "/" + .labels.lag else "" end) severity=\(.labels.severity) pod=\(.labels.pod // "-") startsAt=\(.startsAt)"'; }
am_has() { am_json | jq -e --arg a "$1" 'any(.[]; .labels.alertname == $a and .labels.namespace != "pg-restore")' >/dev/null; }

# wait_alerts STATE TIMEOUT ALERT...: polls Alertmanager every 5 s until every ALERT is firing (STATE=firing) or
# none is (STATE=resolved). Records first-seen and gone times in SEEN_<name> and GONE_<name> (epoch seconds).
wait_alerts() {
  local state=$1 end=$((SECONDS + $2)) a ok cur; shift 2
  while :; do
    cur=$(am_json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[] | select(.labels.namespace != "pg-restore") | .labels.alertname' | sort -u) || cur=
    ok=1
    for a in "$@"; do
      if grep -qx "$a" <<<"$cur"; then [ -n "$(eval echo "\${SEEN_$a:-}")" ] || eval "SEEN_$a=$(date +%s)"
        [ "$state" = firing ] || ok=0
      else [ -z "$(eval echo "\${SEEN_$a:-}")" ] || [ -n "$(eval echo "\${GONE_$a:-}")" ] || eval "GONE_$a=$(date +%s)"
        [ "$state" = resolved ] || ok=0
      fi
    done
    [ $ok = 1 ] && return 0
    [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || return 1
    sleep 5
  done
}
# ts EPOCH: UTC clock time, or n/a
ts() { [ -n "${1:-}" ] && date -u -d "@$1" +%H:%M:%S || echo n/a; }
# Seconds between two epochs, or n/a
dt() { [ -n "${1:-}" ] && [ -n "${2:-}" ] && echo $(( $2 - $1 )) || echo n/a; }

l5_finish() { # part title description make-target
  local verdict=PASS; [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ] || verdict=FAIL
  { printf '# L5: %s\n\n**Result: %s**\n\n' "$2" "$verdict"
    printf -- '- **What:** %s\n' "$3"
    printf -- '- **Run:** %s (UTC), %s s\n- **Reproduce:** `make %s`\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))" "$4"
    printf -- '- **Versions:** Prometheus `%s`, Alertmanager `%s`, postgres_exporter `%s`, image `%s`\n' "${PROMETHEUS_IMAGE%%@*}" "${ALERTMANAGER_IMAGE%%@*}" "${POSTGRES_EXPORTER_IMAGE%%@*}" "$PG_IMAGE"
    [ ! -f "$EV_DIR/L5-monitoring-history.md" ] || printf -- '- **History:** [`L5-monitoring-history.md`](../L5-monitoring-history.md) (maintained by hand)\n'
    printf '\n## Checks\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n'; cat "$CHECKS"; cat "$BODY"; } | redact > "$EV_DIR/L5/$1.md"
  "$ROOT_DIR/tests/l5-summary.sh"
  log "RESULT L5 $1: $verdict -> docs/evidence/L5/$1.md"
  rm -f "$BODY" "$CHECKS"
  [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L5 T:metrics (R10.1), lag measurement (R1.7) and the lag alert on a real fault (R10.3). Then RAM and disk use.
#   1. every scrape target is up, the key series exist, all rules are loaded and healthy;
#   2. no warning or critical alert is firing on the healthy cluster; nothing from pg-restore is scraped;
#   3. induced lag: the async standby's replication stream is throttled while the probe writes. Lag in bytes and
#      seconds must rise above the alert thresholds, ReplicationLagHigh must fire in Alertmanager, and after the
#      throttle is removed lag must return to near zero and the alert resolve.
#
# Fault injection (D4): docker exec <primary's k3d agent> iptables. Two FORWARD rules on the primary's node let
# through at most LIMIT packets/s from the primary pod's port 5432 to the async standby pod and drop the rest, so
# the stream slows down but the connection stays up (a full block would end it after wal_sender_timeout, 60 s,
# and remove the pg_stat_replication row). Both rules are removed on exit.
. "$(dirname "$0")/l5-lib.sh"
LIMIT=${LIMIT:-40}; HOLD=${HOLD:-200}
NODE=; RULES=
cleanup() {
  [ -z "$RULES" ] || { docker exec "$NODE" iptables -D FORWARD $RULES -j DROP 2>/dev/null || true
                       docker exec "$NODE" iptables -D FORWARD $RULES -m limit --limit "$LIMIT/sec" --limit-burst "$LIMIT" -j ACCEPT 2>/dev/null || true; }
  kill "${WRITER:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$BODY" "$CHECKS"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
client_up

section "Scrape targets (R10.1)"
TGT=$(kubectl get --raw "$SVC/prometheus:9090/proxy/api/v1/targets?state=active")
run "jq -r '.data.activeTargets[] | \"\(.labels.job) \(.labels.instance) \(.health)\"' <<<'$(jq -c . <<<"$TGT")' | sort"
NODES=$(kubectl get nodes --no-headers | wc -l)
for j in patroni:3 postgres:3 node:$NODES kube-state-metrics:1 alertmanager:1 prometheus:1; do
  n=$(jq --arg j "${j%:*}" '[.data.activeTargets[] | select(.labels.job == $j and .health == "up")] | length' <<<"$TGT")
  check "Job ${j%:*}: ${j#*:} target(s) up (found $n)" test "$n" = "${j#*:}"
done
check "No target is down" test "$(jq '[.data.activeTargets[] | select(.health != "up")] | length' <<<"$TGT")" = 0

section "Key series (R10.1)"
note "One query per signal that an alert or the lag measurement depends on. Values at the time of the run."
key() { # description query expected-min-series
  local out n; out=$(promq "$2" 2>/dev/null) || out=; n=$(grep -c . <<<"$out" || true)
  printf '\n`%s`\n\n```\n%s\n```\n' "$2" "${out:-(no series)}" >> "$BODY"
  check "$1: $n series (need $3)" test "$n" -ge "$3"
}
key "Patroni role per member" 'patroni_primary{namespace="pg-ha"}' 3
key "Exactly one primary" 'sum(patroni_primary{namespace="pg-ha"}) == 1' 1
key "Sync standby flag" 'sum(patroni_sync_standby{namespace="pg-ha"}) == 1' 1
key "Postgres reachable by each exporter" 'pg_up{namespace="pg-ha"} == 1' 3
key "Timeline" 'patroni_postgres_timeline{namespace="pg-ha"}' 3
key "Replication lag in bytes per standby (primary's view)" 'pg_ha_replication_lag_bytes{namespace="pg-ha"}' 2
key "Replication lag in seconds per standby (primary's view)" 'pg_ha_replication_replay_lag_seconds{namespace="pg-ha"}' 2
key "Slot WAL retention" 'pg_ha_slot_retained_bytes{namespace="pg-ha"}' 2
key "Archiver failure counter" 'pg_stat_archiver_failed_count{namespace="pg-ha"}' 3
key "Archive backlog (.ready)" 'pg_ha_archive_oldest_ready_seconds{namespace="pg-ha"}' 3
key "Backup and restore-test CronJobs" 'kube_cronjob_created{namespace="pg-ha"}' 2
key "Backup or restore-test Job status" 'kube_job_status_succeeded{namespace="pg-ha", job_name=~"pg-backup-.+|pg-restore-test.*"}' 1
key "Expected member count" 'kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace="pg-ha", statefulset="pg"}' 1
key "CoreDNS availability" 'kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="kube-system", deployment="coredns"}' 1
key "Root filesystem free space per node" 'node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint="/"}' "$NODES"
RESTORE=$(promq 'count({namespace="pg-restore"})')
check "No series from namespace pg-restore is scraped" test -z "$RESTORE"

section "Rules"
RULES_JSON=$(kubectl get --raw "$SVC/prometheus:9090/proxy/api/v1/rules")
run "jq -r '.data.groups[] | .name as \$g | .rules[] | \"\(\$g) \(.name) \(.health) \(.state)\"' <<<'$(jq -c . <<<"$RULES_JSON")'"
check "19 alerting rules loaded" test "$(jq '[.data.groups[].rules[] | select(.type == "alerting")] | length' <<<"$RULES_JSON")" = 19
check "Every rule evaluates without error" test "$(jq '[.data.groups[].rules[] | select(.health != "ok")] | length' <<<"$RULES_JSON")" = 0
section "Alerts on the healthy cluster"
TAIL=20 run "am_lines"
check "No warning or critical alert firing before the fault" test "$(am_json | jq '[.[] | select(.labels.severity != "info")] | length')" = 0

section "Induced lag (R1.7, R10.3)"
PRIMARY=$(leader); NODE=$(pod_node "$PRIMARY"); P_IP=$(pod_ip "$PRIMARY")
ASYNC=$(q "$RW" monitor "select application_name from pg_stat_replication where sync_state = 'async' limit 1")
[ -n "$ASYNC" ] || die "no async standby"
A_IP=$(pod_ip "$ASYNC")
note "Primary \`$PRIMARY\` on \`$NODE\`, async standby \`$ASYNC\`. Its stream is limited to $LIMIT packets/s for $HOLD s while a writer fills WAL through pg-rw (one 16 MB+ fill every 10 s). Lag is read from Prometheus, which is what the alerts use."
LAG_Q="pg_ha_replication_lag_bytes{namespace=\"pg-ha\",application_name=\"$ASYNC\"}"
SEC_Q="pg_ha_replication_replay_lag_seconds{namespace=\"pg-ha\",application_name=\"$ASYNC\"}"
B0=$(promv "$LAG_Q"); S0=$(promv "$SEC_Q")
RULES="-s $P_IP -d $A_IP -p tcp --sport 5432"
T_FAULT=$(date +%s)
docker exec "$NODE" iptables -I FORWARD 1 $RULES -j DROP
docker exec "$NODE" iptables -I FORWARD 1 $RULES -m limit --limit "$LIMIT/sec" --limit-burst "$LIMIT" -j ACCEPT
( while :; do wal_fill >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; sleep 10; done ) & WRITER=$!
wait_alerts firing "$HOLD" ReplicationLagHigh && FIRED=1 || FIRED=0
LAG_FIRING=$(am_lines | grep ReplicationLagHigh || true)
BMAX=$(promv "max_over_time(${LAG_Q}[10m])"); SMAX=$(promv "max_over_time(${SEC_Q}[10m])")
STREAMING=$(q "$RW" monitor "select state from pg_stat_replication where application_name = '$ASYNC'")
kill "$WRITER" 2>/dev/null || true; wait "$WRITER" 2>/dev/null || true; WRITER=
docker exec "$NODE" iptables -D FORWARD $RULES -j DROP
docker exec "$NODE" iptables -D FORWARD $RULES -m limit --limit "$LIMIT/sec" --limit-burst "$LIMIT" -j ACCEPT
RULES=; T_CLEAR=$(date +%s)
# Back to near zero: under 1 MiB and under 1 s, as scraped.
end=$((SECONDS + 180)); T_ZERO=
while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do
  b=$(promv "$LAG_Q"); s=$(promv "$SEC_Q")
  awk -v b="${b:-1e18}" -v s="${s:-1e9}" 'BEGIN{exit !(b < 1048576 && s < 1)}' && { T_ZERO=$(date +%s); break; }
  sleep 5
done
B1=$(promv "$LAG_Q"); S1=$(promv "$SEC_Q")
wait_alerts resolved 300 ReplicationLagHigh && RESOLVED=1 || RESOLVED=0
cat >> "$BODY" <<EOF

<!-- summary -->
| Measure | Before | Peak during throttle | After |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Lag bytes ($ASYNC) | ${B0:-n/a} | ${BMAX:-n/a} | ${B1:-n/a} |
| Lag seconds ($ASYNC) | ${S0:-n/a} | ${SMAX:-n/a} | ${S1:-n/a} |

| Event | Time (UTC) | Seconds after throttle start |
|---|---|---:|
| Throttle on | $(ts "$T_FAULT") | 0 |
| ReplicationLagHigh first seen firing | $(ts "${SEEN_ReplicationLagHigh:-}") | $(dt "$T_FAULT" "${SEEN_ReplicationLagHigh:-}") |
| Throttle off | $(ts "$T_CLEAR") | $(dt "$T_FAULT" "$T_CLEAR") |
| Lag back under 1 MiB and 1 s | $(ts "$T_ZERO") | $(dt "$T_FAULT" "$T_ZERO") |
| ReplicationLagHigh gone from Alertmanager | $(ts "${GONE_ReplicationLagHigh:-}") | $(dt "$T_FAULT" "${GONE_ReplicationLagHigh:-}") |
<!-- /summary -->

Alertmanager while firing:

\`\`\`
${LAG_FIRING:-(none)}
\`\`\`
EOF
check "Lag in bytes rose above the 16 MiB threshold (peak ${BMAX:-n/a})" awk -v v="${BMAX:-0}" 'BEGIN{exit !(v > 16777216)}'
check "Lag in seconds rose above the 30 s threshold (peak ${SMAX:-n/a})" awk -v v="${SMAX:-0}" 'BEGIN{exit !(v > 30)}'
check "The standby stayed connected during the throttle (state ${STREAMING:-none})" test -n "$STREAMING"
check "ReplicationLagHigh fired in Alertmanager" test "$FIRED" = 1
check "Lag returned to near zero (< 1 MiB, < 1 s) within 180 s of removing the throttle" test -n "$T_ZERO"
check "ReplicationLagHigh resolved in Alertmanager" test "$RESOLVED" = 1

section "Resources with monitoring running"
note "Measured after the lag test. Memory per component is the resident set of its main process, as each one reports it (process_resident_memory_bytes). The host has no metrics-server (k3s's is disabled, ADR-001), so pod memory comes from these metrics and from docker stats on the k3d node containers."
run "promq 'sum by (job) (process_resident_memory_bytes)'"
run "promq 'prometheus_tsdb_head_series'"
run "promq 'sum(prometheus_tsdb_storage_blocks_bytes) + sum(prometheus_tsdb_wal_storage_size_bytes) + sum(prometheus_tsdb_head_chunks_storage_size_bytes)'"
run "docker stats --no-stream --format '{{.Name}} {{.MemUsage}} {{.CPUPerc}}' \$(docker ps -q --filter name=k3d-$CLUSTER_NAME)"
run "free -m"
run "df -h /"
RSS=$(promq 'sum by (job) (process_resident_memory_bytes)' | awk '{split($1,a,"="); printf "| %s | %.0f MiB |\n", a[2], $2/1048576}')
TSDB=$(promv 'sum(prometheus_tsdb_storage_blocks_bytes) + sum(prometheus_tsdb_wal_storage_size_bytes) + sum(prometheus_tsdb_head_chunks_storage_size_bytes)')
cat >> "$BODY" <<EOF

<!-- summary -->
| Component (job) | Resident memory |
|---|---:|
$RSS
| Prometheus TSDB on disk | $(awk -v v="${TSDB:-0}" 'BEGIN{printf "%.0f MiB", v/1048576}') |
| Host memory used / total | $(free -m | awk '/^Mem:/{print $3 " / " $2 " MiB"}') |
| Host disk used / size (/) | $(df -h / | awk 'NR==2{print $3 " / " $2 " (" $5 ")"}') |
<!-- /summary -->
EOF
l5_finish metrics "Scrape targets, key series, lag measurement and resources (R10.1, R1.7)" \
  "Every scrape target up, the key series for each alert present, all rules loaded and healthy, nothing firing on the healthy cluster, nothing scraped from pg-restore. Then induced lag (R1.7): the async standby's stream is throttled with iptables on the primary's node while a writer fills WAL. Lag in bytes and seconds must rise past the alert thresholds, ReplicationLagHigh must fire in Alertmanager (R10.3), and after the throttle lag must return to near zero and the alert resolve. Then RAM and disk use with monitoring running." test-metrics

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L5 R10.3, scenario a: node failover. The primary's k3d agent is stopped for DOWN s (default 180), then started.
# Expected in Alertmanager: MemberDown (the old primary), ReplicaNotStreaming and FailoverOccurred fire, then all
# three resolve after the node returns and the member rejoins. NoPrimary and MultiplePrimaries must stay silent,
# because Patroni fails over within 45 s (L2: 26 s at worst) and fences the old primary.
#
# Fault injection (D4): docker stop / docker start of the k3d agent container, as in make failover-node. No exec.
# DOWN is longer than in L2, where the node returns as soon as a new leader holds the lock, so that the 30 s and
# 2 min alert delays elapse while the member is really gone.
. "$(dirname "$0")/l5-lib.sh"
DOWN=${DOWN:-180}; NODE=
cleanup() { [ -z "$NODE" ] || docker start "$NODE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; rm -f "$BODY" "$CHECKS"; }
trap cleanup EXIT
client_up
patroni_healthy || die "Patroni not healthy before the test"
EXPECT="MemberDown ReplicaNotStreaming FailoverOccurred"

section "Before"
OLD=$(leader); NODE=$(pod_node "$OLD"); TL0=$(promv 'max(patroni_postgres_timeline{namespace="pg-ha"})')
TAIL=10 run "am_lines"
check "No warning or critical alert firing before the fault" test "$(am_json | jq '[.[] | select(.labels.severity != "info")] | length')" = 0
note "Primary \`$OLD\` on \`$NODE\`, timeline $TL0. CoreDNS on: $(coredns_nodes)."

section "Fault"
T_FAULT=$(date +%s); docker stop "$NODE" >/dev/null
note "\`docker stop $NODE\` at $(ts "$T_FAULT") UTC. Held for $DOWN s."
T_NEW=; NEW=
end=$((SECONDS + DOWN)); NP=0; MP=0
while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do
  [ -n "$T_NEW" ] || { l=$(leader); [ -n "$l" ] && [ "$l" != "$OLD" ] && { NEW=$l; T_NEW=$(date +%s); }; }
  am_has NoPrimary && NP=1; am_has MultiplePrimaries && MP=1
  wait_alerts firing 0 $EXPECT >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  sleep 5
done
section "Alertmanager at the end of the outage (make alerts)"
TAIL=20 run "scripts/alerts.sh"
FIRING=$(am_json)
for a in MemberDown ReplicaNotStreaming; do
  check "$a firing while the node is down" jq -e --arg a "$a" 'any(.[]; .labels.alertname == $a)' <<<"$FIRING"
done
check "MemberDown names the old primary $OLD" jq -e --arg p "$OLD" 'any(.[]; .labels.alertname == "MemberDown" and .labels.pod == $p)' <<<"$FIRING"
check "FailoverOccurred fired (new primary ${NEW:-none})" test -n "${SEEN_FailoverOccurred:-}"
check "A new primary took over (${NEW:-none}, $(dt "$T_FAULT" "$T_NEW") s after the fault)" test -n "$NEW"

section "Recovery"
T_START=$(date +%s); docker start "$NODE" >/dev/null; NODE_STARTED=$NODE; NODE=
end=$((SECONDS + 300)); T_HEALTHY=
while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do patroni_healthy && { T_HEALTHY=$(date +%s); break; }; am_has NoPrimary && NP=1; am_has MultiplePrimaries && MP=1; sleep 3; done
check "Cluster healthy again: 1 leader, 2 streaming, 1 sync ($(dt "$T_START" "$T_HEALTHY") s after docker start)" test -n "$T_HEALTHY"
# FailoverOccurred clears 5 min after the promotion; the others once the member streams again.
wait_alerts resolved 600 $EXPECT && RES=1 || RES=0
am_has NoPrimary && NP=1; am_has MultiplePrimaries && MP=1
check "MemberDown, ReplicaNotStreaming and FailoverOccurred all resolved" test "$RES" = 1
check "NoPrimary never fired (failover finished within its 45 s delay)" test "$NP" = 0
check "MultiplePrimaries never fired" test "$MP" = 0
TAIL=10 run "am_lines"
check "No warning or critical alert firing at the end" test "$(am_json | jq '[.[] | select(.labels.severity != "info")] | length')" = 0
run "patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | \"\(.name) role=\(.role) state=\(.state) timeline=\(.timeline)\"'"

row() { printf '| %s | %s | %s | %s | %s |\n' "$1" "$(ts "$(eval echo "\${SEEN_$1:-}")")" "$(dt "$T_FAULT" "$(eval echo "\${SEEN_$1:-}")")" "$(ts "$(eval echo "\${GONE_$1:-}")")" "$(dt "$T_FAULT" "$(eval echo "\${GONE_$1:-}")")"; }
cat >> "$BODY" <<EOF

## Timeline

Times are UTC. Alertmanager was polled every 5 s through the API server's service proxy, so each time is accurate to about 5 s. Alert delays add the scrape interval (10 s), the rule evaluation interval (10 s) and Alertmanager's group_wait (10 s) to each rule's \`for\`.

<!-- summary -->
| Event | Time | Seconds after fault |
|---|---|---:|
| docker stop $NODE_STARTED (primary $OLD) | $(ts "$T_FAULT") | 0 |
| New primary $NEW holds the lock | $(ts "$T_NEW") | $(dt "$T_FAULT" "$T_NEW") |
| docker start | $(ts "$T_START") | $(dt "$T_FAULT" "$T_START") |
| Cluster healthy (3 members, sync standby) | $(ts "$T_HEALTHY") | $(dt "$T_FAULT" "$T_HEALTHY") |

| Alert | First seen firing | s after fault | Gone | s after fault |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
$(row MemberDown)
$(row ReplicaNotStreaming)
$(row FailoverOccurred)
<!-- /summary -->

Alertmanager's full alert objects at the end of the outage:

\`\`\`json
$(jq '[.[] | {alertname: .labels.alertname, severity: .labels.severity, pod: .labels.pod, startsAt, summary: .annotations.summary}]' <<<"$FIRING")
\`\`\`
EOF
l5_finish alerts-failover "Alerts on a node failover (R10.3)" \
  "\`docker stop\` of the primary's k3d agent for $DOWN s, then \`docker start\`. MemberDown, ReplicaNotStreaming and FailoverOccurred must fire in Alertmanager and then resolve. NoPrimary and MultiplePrimaries must stay silent. Read from the Alertmanager API through the API server's service proxy." alerts-failover

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L5 R10.3 and R9.6, scenario b: object-storage outage for the primary. The primary pod's traffic to Garage is
# dropped for up to HOLD s while a writer fills WAL. Expected: writes continue, ArchiveFailing and ArchiveStale
# fire in Alertmanager; after the block is removed, archiving catches up with no .ready segment left behind and
# both alerts resolve.
#
# Fault injection (D4): docker exec <primary's k3d agent> iptables. One FORWARD rule on the primary's node drops
# TCP from the primary pod's IP to the Garage pod's IP on port 3900 (the S3 API). The Service address is
# translated to the pod address before FORWARD, so the rule sees the real backend (the S2 finding). Removed on exit.
. "$(dirname "$0")/l5-lib.sh"
HOLD=${HOLD:-420}; NODE=; RULE=
cleanup() { [ -z "$RULE" ] || docker exec "$NODE" iptables -D FORWARD $RULE -j DROP 2>/dev/null || true
            kill "${WRITER:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true; rm -f "$BODY" "$CHECKS" "${WLOG:-}"; }
trap cleanup EXIT
client_up
patroni_healthy || die "Patroni not healthy before the test"
EXPECT="ArchiveFailing ArchiveStale"

section "Before"
PRIMARY=$(leader); NODE=$(pod_node "$PRIMARY"); P_IP=$(pod_ip "$PRIMARY")
G_IP=$(kubectl -n "$NS" get pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=garage -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.podIP}')
[ -n "$G_IP" ] || die "Garage pod IP not found"
S0=$(archive_stat "$RW"); F0=$(awk '{print $1}' <<<"$S0")
run "echo 'failed_count last_archived_epoch last_archived_wal ready_count ready_names'; archive_stat $RW"
TAIL=10 run "am_lines"
check "No warning or critical alert firing before the fault" test "$(am_json | jq '[.[] | select(.labels.severity != "info")] | length')" = 0
note "Primary \`$PRIMARY\` ($P_IP) on \`$NODE\`. Garage pod $G_IP:3900."

section "Fault"
RULE="-s $P_IP -d $G_IP -p tcp --dport 3900"
T_FAULT=$(date +%s); docker exec "$NODE" iptables -I FORWARD 1 $RULE -j DROP
note "Rule on \`$NODE\`: \`iptables -I FORWARD 1 $RULE -j DROP\` at $(ts "$T_FAULT") UTC. A writer fills one 16 MB+ WAL segment through pg-rw every 15 s."
WLOG=$(mktemp)
( while :; do if wal_fill >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo ok; else echo fail; fi; sleep 15; done >> "$WLOG" ) & WRITER=$!
wait_alerts firing "$HOLD" $EXPECT && FIRED=1 || FIRED=0
section "Alertmanager during the outage (make alerts)"
TAIL=20 run "scripts/alerts.sh"
FIRING=$(am_json)
SP=$(archive_stat "$RW" || echo "? 0 - ? -")
run "echo 'failed_count last_archived_epoch last_archived_wal ready_count ready_names'; echo '$SP'"
kill "$WRITER" 2>/dev/null || true; wait "$WRITER" 2>/dev/null || true; WRITER=
OKW=$(grep -c ok "$WLOG" || true); FAILW=$(grep -c fail "$WLOG" || true)
check "ArchiveFailing fired" test -n "${SEEN_ArchiveFailing:-}"
check "ArchiveStale fired" test -n "${SEEN_ArchiveStale:-}"
check "Writes continued during the outage ($OKW WAL fills succeeded, $FAILW failed)" test "$OKW" -ge 3 -a "$FAILW" = 0
check "Primary did not change during the outage ($(leader))" test "$(leader)" = "$PRIMARY"
READY_PEAK=$(awk '{print $4}' <<<"$SP"); LAST_READY=$(awk '{print $5}' <<<"$SP" | tr ',' '\n' | sort | tail -1)
check "WAL waited in .ready during the outage ($READY_PEAK segments)" test "${READY_PEAK:-0}" -ge 1 2>/dev/null

section "Recovery"
docker exec "$NODE" iptables -D FORWARD $RULE -j DROP; RULE=; T_CLEAR=$(date +%s)
end=$((SECONDS + 300)); T_CAUGHT=
while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do
  s=$(archive_stat "$RW" 2>/dev/null) || { sleep 3; continue; }
  [ "$(awk '{print $4}' <<<"$s")" = 0 ] && { T_CAUGHT=$(date +%s); break; }; sleep 3
done
S1=$(archive_stat "$RW"); LAST1=$(awk '{print $3}' <<<"$S1")
run "echo 'failed_count last_archived_epoch last_archived_wal ready_count ready_names'; echo '$S1'"
check "Archive caught up: no .ready segment left ($(dt "$T_CLEAR" "$T_CAUGHT") s after unblocking)" test -n "$T_CAUGHT"
check "Last archived segment $LAST1 is at or past the newest segment that waited (${LAST_READY:-none})" \
  test -n "$LAST_READY" -a "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "${LAST_READY:0:24}" "${LAST1:0:24}" | sort | tail -1)" = "${LAST1:0:24}"
archive_check "$RW" "$(awk '{print $1}' <<<"$S1")" "$ARCHIVE_BOUND"
check "A new segment is archived within $ARCHIVE_BOUND s after recovery (${ARCH_T} s, no new failures: $ARCH_FAILED)" test "$ARCH_T" != n/a -a "$ARCH_FAILED" = 0
wait_alerts resolved 600 $EXPECT && RES=1 || RES=0
check "ArchiveFailing and ArchiveStale resolved" test "$RES" = 1
TAIL=10 run "am_lines"
check "No warning or critical alert firing at the end" test "$(am_json | jq '[.[] | select(.labels.severity != "info")] | length')" = 0

row() { printf '| %s | %s | %s | %s | %s |\n' "$1" "$(ts "$(eval echo "\${SEEN_$1:-}")")" "$(dt "$T_FAULT" "$(eval echo "\${SEEN_$1:-}")")" "$(ts "$(eval echo "\${GONE_$1:-}")")" "$(dt "$T_FAULT" "$(eval echo "\${GONE_$1:-}")")"; }
cat >> "$BODY" <<EOF

## Timeline

Times are UTC. Alertmanager was polled every 5 s through the API server's service proxy, so each time is accurate to about 5 s. ArchiveFailing waits for pgBackRest's first failed archive-push. With dropped packets that is its io-timeout (60 s). ArchiveFailing then clears 5 min after the last failure, because its window is 5 min.

<!-- summary -->
| Event | Time | Seconds after fault |
|---|---|---:|
| Primary $PRIMARY blocked from Garage | $(ts "$T_FAULT") | 0 |
| Block removed | $(ts "$T_CLEAR") | $(dt "$T_FAULT" "$T_CLEAR") |
| No .ready segment left (caught up) | $(ts "$T_CAUGHT") | $(dt "$T_FAULT" "$T_CAUGHT") |

| Alert | First seen firing | s after fault | Gone | s after fault |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
$(row ArchiveFailing)
$(row ArchiveStale)

Archiver failures during the test: $(( $(awk '{print $1}' <<<"$S1") - F0 )). Segments waiting at the end of the outage: ${READY_PEAK:-n/a}.
<!-- /summary -->

Alertmanager's alert objects during the outage:

\`\`\`json
$(jq '[.[] | {alertname: .labels.alertname, severity: .labels.severity, pod: .labels.pod, startsAt, summary: .annotations.summary}]' <<<"$FIRING")
\`\`\`
EOF
l5_finish alerts-archive "Alerts on an object-storage outage (R10.3, R9.6)" \
  "The primary pod's traffic to Garage is dropped with iptables on its node while a writer fills WAL. Writes must continue, ArchiveFailing and ArchiveStale must fire in Alertmanager, and after the block is removed archiving must catch up with no segment left waiting and both alerts resolve." alerts-archive

# Observability (L5)

Monitoring and alerting for the `pg-ha` cluster, built from our own manifests, with no operators or charts (ADR-011, D1, D2). Covers R1.6, R1.7, R10.1, R10.2, R10.3 and R10.5. Evidence: [`evidence/L5-monitoring.md`](evidence/L5-monitoring.md).

## What runs where

| Component | Where | Image (versions.env) | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prometheus | `monitoring`, server node | `PROMETHEUS_IMAGE` | Scrapes every 10 s, evaluates rules every 10 s, keeps 3 days (max 1 GB) in an emptyDir |
| Alertmanager | `monitoring`, server node | `ALERTMANAGER_IMAGE` | Groups alerts. Uses a no-op receiver, so nothing is sent and no secret exists |
| kube-state-metrics | `monitoring`, server node | `KUBE_STATE_METRICS_IMAGE` | Job, CronJob, StatefulSet and Deployment state in `pg-ha` and `kube-system` only |
| node_exporter | `monitoring-host`, every node (DaemonSet) | `NODE_EXPORTER_IMAGE` | Root filesystem space, memory, load |
| postgres_exporter | sidecar `exporter` in each `pg-N` pod | `POSTGRES_EXPORTER_IMAGE` | Built-in Postgres metrics plus three custom queries ([`deploy/pg/exporter/queries.yaml`](../deploy/pg/exporter/queries.yaml)) |
| Patroni `/metrics` | each `pg-N` pod, port 8008 | (our image) | Role, timeline, streaming state, sync standby |

Deployed by `make monitoring`, which is part of `make up`. The exporter sidecar is part of the StatefulSet (`make deploy`). Manifests are in [`deploy/monitoring/`](../deploy/monitoring/).

**RBAC (least privilege, Roles only, no ClusterRole):**
- Prometheus can get, list and watch pods in `pg-ha` and `monitoring-host`, for service discovery. Every other target is static.
- kube-state-metrics can list and watch Jobs, CronJobs, StatefulSets and Deployments in `pg-ha` and `kube-system`. kube-state-metrics watches each listed resource in each listed namespace, so the two Roles are identical.
- Alertmanager and node_exporter have no API token mounted.

**Pod Security.** `monitoring` enforces `restricted`. node_exporter needs a read-only `hostPath` mount of the node's root for disk space, which `baseline` and `restricted` both forbid. It therefore runs alone in `monitoring-host`, which enforces `privileged` and warns and audits at `restricted`. This is a documented exception for R8.7. The pod still runs as non-root (65534) with no capabilities, no privilege escalation, a read-only root filesystem, and no hostNetwork or hostPID.

## What is scraped

| Job | Targets | Discovery | Key series |
|---|---|---|---|
| `patroni` | 3 members, `:8008/metrics` | pods in `pg-ha` with `app.kubernetes.io/name=pg` | `patroni_primary`, `patroni_postgres_running`, `patroni_postgres_streaming`, `patroni_sync_standby`, `patroni_postgres_timeline`, `patroni_xlog_*` |
| `postgres` | 3 members, `:9187` | same pods, port `metrics` | `pg_up`, `pg_replication_is_replica`, `pg_stat_archiver_*`, `pg_ha_archive_*`, `pg_ha_replication_*`, `pg_ha_slot_*` |
| `node` | every node, `:9100` | pods in `monitoring-host` | `node_filesystem_avail_bytes`, `node_filesystem_size_bytes`, `node_memory_*` |
| `kube-state-metrics` | 1 | static Service | `kube_job_*`, `kube_cronjob_created`, `kube_statefulset_replicas`, `kube_deployment_status_replicas_available` |
| `alertmanager`, `prometheus` | 1 each | static | `up`, process metrics |

Every target gets `namespace`, `pod` and `node` labels from discovery. Only `pg-ha` is discovered, so a restored cluster in `pg-restore` is never scraped. Every Postgres, backup and restore rule also selects `namespace="pg-ha"`, which `make test-alerts` checks. Its unit tests include `pg-restore` series that must not fire.

**Custom exporter queries** (all work on a primary and on a standby):

| Metric | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pg_ha_archive_ready_count`, `pg_ha_archive_oldest_ready_seconds` | WAL segments waiting to be archived (`.ready` files from `pg_ls_archive_statusdir()`), and the age of the oldest one |
| `pg_ha_replication_lag_bytes`, `pg_ha_replication_replay_lag_seconds` | Per standby, from the primary's `pg_stat_replication` (labels `application_name`, `state`, `sync_state`) |
| `pg_ha_slot_retained_bytes`, `pg_ha_slot_safe_wal_size_bytes`, `pg_ha_slot_lost`, `pg_ha_slot_active` | Per replication slot, from `pg_replication_slots` |

## How replication lag is measured (R1.7)

Lag is read on the primary, per standby, from `pg_stat_replication`. The exporter runs this query every 10 s:

```sql
select application_name, state, sync_state,
       case when pg_is_in_recovery() then 0 else pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), replay_lsn) end as lag_bytes,
       coalesce(extract(epoch from replay_lag), 0) as replay_lag_seconds
from pg_stat_replication where replay_lsn is not null
```

- **Bytes** is how much WAL the primary has written that the standby has not replayed yet.
- **Seconds** is Postgres's own `replay_lag`: the time between the primary flushing WAL and the standby reporting it replayed. Postgres shows NULL once a standby has caught up and nothing new is written, so NULL is reported as 0.

PromQL used by the alerts and by `make test-metrics`:

```promql
# Lag in bytes per standby
max by (application_name) (pg_ha_replication_lag_bytes{namespace="pg-ha"})
# Lag in seconds per standby
max by (application_name) (pg_ha_replication_replay_lag_seconds{namespace="pg-ha"})
# Cross-check from Patroni, bytes: primary's WAL position minus each standby's replayed position
scalar(max(patroni_xlog_location{namespace="pg-ha"} * on (pod) patroni_primary{namespace="pg-ha"}))
  - on () group_right patroni_xlog_replayed_location{namespace="pg-ha"} * on (pod) (patroni_replica{namespace="pg-ha"} == 1)
```

`make test-metrics` shows lag rising under a throttled stream and returning to near zero. The values are in the evidence.

## Alerts

Rules: [`deploy/monitoring/rules/pg-ha.rules.yml`](../deploy/monitoring/rules/pg-ha.rules.yml). Unit tests: [`tests/alerts/pg-ha.test.yml`](../tests/alerts/pg-ha.test.yml) (`make test-alerts`, 33 test groups, each alert both fires and stays silent). Severities: **critical** means data or availability is at risk now. **warning** means degraded, act today. **info** is a record only.

| Alert | Severity | Condition (summary) | Threshold | Why this threshold | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NoPrimary | critical | No member has `patroni_primary = 1`, or no Patroni metrics at all | for 45 s | Worst measured failover is 26 s (L2 node mode). 45 s means failover itself failed | `make status`. Check the DCS (API server) and CoreDNS, then Patroni logs on the members |
| MultiplePrimaries | critical | More than one `patroni_primary = 1`, or more than one Postgres not in recovery | for 20 s | One scrape can catch both during a switchover. Two evaluations rule that out | Stop client writes and find the member without the leader lock. See the L2 split-brain evidence |
| MemberDown | warning | Patroni scrape fails, Postgres not running, or fewer `up` members than StatefulSet replicas | for 30 s | Pod restart takes 10–20 s and ttl is 20 s. Still serving on two members | `kubectl get pods -o wide`, node state, Patroni logs |
| ReplicaNotStreaming | warning | Fewer streaming standbys than replicas − 1 | for 2 min | Re-clone takes about 1 min at this size (ADR-008, L4). Raise it as data grows | Look for a re-clone in Patroni logs, a lost slot, or a network problem |
| ReplicationLagHigh (`lag=bytes`) | warning | A standby's lag in bytes > 16 MiB | for 2 min | Above 1 MiB (`maximum_lag_on_failover`) it cannot be promoted. 2 min filters bulk loads | Check standby I/O and network, and long queries on the standby |
| ReplicationLagHigh (`lag=seconds`) | warning | A standby's `replay_lag` > 30 s | for 2 min | Equals the RTO target, because a promoted standby would replay that much first | As above |
| SyncStandbyMissing | critical | A primary exists, but no member is sync standby | for 1 min | Non-strict sync (ADR-004): commits are not replicated, and Patroni will not fail over automatically. A new sync is normally picked within seconds | Bring a standby back to streaming (see ReplicaNotStreaming) |
| SlotWALRetentionHigh | warning | A slot holds > 512 MiB of WAL | for 5 min | Half of `max_slot_wal_keep_size` (1 GB, ADR-005) | Find the inactive or lagging standby before the slot is invalidated |
| SlotLost | warning | A slot's `wal_status` is `lost` | immediate | The 1 GB cap was hit. The standby needs the archive or a re-clone | Confirm the standby recovered through `restore_command`, otherwise re-clone it |
| ArchiveFailing | warning | `pg_stat_archiver.failed_count` increased in the last 5 min | immediate | Any failure means WAL is not leaving. One failed attempt during a Garage restart warns and clears | Check Garage, and the archive-push error in the Postgres log |

| `node` | every node, `:9100` | pods in `monitoring-host` | `node_filesystem_avail_bytes`, `node_filesystem_size_bytes`, `node_memory_*` |
| `kube-state-metrics` | 1 | static Service | `kube_job_*`, `kube_cronjob_created`, `kube_statefulset_replicas`, `kube_deployment_status_replicas_available` |

| MultiplePrimaries | critical | More than one `patroni_primary = 1`, or more than one Postgres not in recovery | for 20 s | One scrape can catch both during a switchover. Two evaluations rule that out | Stop client writes and find the member without the leader lock. See the L2 split-brain evidence |
| MemberDown | warning | Patroni scrape fails, Postgres not running, or fewer `up` members than StatefulSet replicas | for 30 s | Pod restart takes 10–20 s and ttl is 20 s. Still serving on two members | `kubectl get pods -o wide`, node state, Patroni logs |
| ReplicaNotStreaming | warning | Fewer streaming standbys than replicas − 1 | for 2 min | Re-clone takes about 1 min at this size (ADR-008, L4). Raise it as data grows | Look for a re-clone in Patroni logs, a lost slot, or a network problem |
| ReplicationLagHigh (`lag=bytes`) | warning | A standby's lag in bytes > 16 MiB | for 2 min | Above 1 MiB (`maximum_lag_on_failover`) it cannot be promoted. 2 min filters bulk loads | Check standby I/O and network, and long queries on the standby |
| ReplicationLagHigh (`lag=seconds`) | warning | A standby's `replay_lag` > 30 s | for 2 min | Equals the RTO target, because a promoted standby would replay that much first | As above |
| SyncStandbyMissing | critical | A primary exists, but no member is sync standby | for 1 min | Non-strict sync (ADR-004): commits are not replicated, and Patroni will not fail over automatically. A new sync is normally picked within seconds | Bring a standby back to streaming (see ReplicaNotStreaming) |
| SlotWALRetentionHigh | warning | A slot holds > 512 MiB of WAL | for 5 min | Half of `max_slot_wal_keep_size` (1 GB, ADR-005) | Find the inactive or lagging standby before the slot is invalidated |
| SlotLost | warning | A slot's `wal_status` is `lost` | immediate | The 1 GB cap was hit. The standby needs the archive or a re-clone | Confirm the standby recovered through `restore_command`, otherwise re-clone it |
| ArchiveFailing | warning | `pg_stat_archiver.failed_count` increased in the last 5 min | immediate | Any failure means WAL is not leaving. One failed attempt during a Garage restart warns and clears | Check Garage, and the archive-push error in the Postgres log |
| ArchiveStale | critical | Oldest `.ready` WAL segment waiting > 120 s | immediate | A segment closes ≤ 60 s (`archive_timeout`) after its first write, and a Garage restart adds about 60 s. Beyond that, more than 3 min of writes is not in the repository. Idle clusters close no segment, so they do not fire | As ArchiveFailing. PITR (RPO) is degrading |
| BackupFailed | warning | The newest `pg-backup-*` Job failed (newer than the newest success) | immediate | The Job exits non-zero on backup, expire or verify errors | Read the Job log, then `make backup` |
| BackupStale | critical | No `pg-backup-*` Job succeeded in 26 h (new clusters get 26 h from CronJob creation) | 26 h | Daily at 20:00 UTC. 26 h allows a late run, not a missed day | Check the CronJob and the last Job, then `make backup` |
| RestoreTestFailed | warning | The newest `pg-restore-test*` Job failed | immediate | It exits non-zero on restore, recovery or `pg_amcheck` errors (ADR-010) | Read the Job log. The newest backup may not be restorable |
| RestoreTestStale | warning | No `pg-restore-test*` Job succeeded in 26 h | 26 h | Daily at 21:00 UTC | Check the CronJob, then `make test-restore` |
| DiskLow | warning | Root filesystem free < 15 % on a node | for 5 min | local-path volumes are not size-limited, so data, WAL, the restore test (≤ 4 Gi) and the slot cap share the 48 GB host. 15 % is about 7 GB | Free space or grow the disk, and check slot retention |
| CoreDNSNotReady | critical | CoreDNS Deployment has no available replica | for 1 min | Promotion runs `restore_command`, which resolves Garage through DNS (L3). A restart takes 10–20 s | Check the server node and the CoreDNS pod |
| FailoverOccurred | info | Highest timeline is above its value 5 min ago | immediate, clears after 5 min | Informational. Every promotion (failover or switchover) starts a timeline | Confirm the failover was expected, and check the old primary rejoined |
| MonitoringTargetDown | warning | kube-state-metrics, node_exporter or Alertmanager scrape down | for 5 min | Backup, restore, CoreDNS and disk alerts are blind without them. 5 min tolerates a restart | Restart the component (`make monitoring`) |

**Design notes**
- **BackupStale and RestoreTestStale count only Jobs named `pg-backup-*` / `pg-restore-test*`.** The CronJob's `lastSuccessfulTime` is not used. Stanza and check Jobs made from the `pg-backup` template are owned by that CronJob and set it too, so it would hide a missing backup. This was seen live during L5.
- **ArchiveStale uses the age of the oldest `.ready` file, not `last_archived_time`.** A quiet primary writes no WAL and closes no segment, so `last_archived_time` grows forever without any data at risk. Standbys also keep the archiver counters from their time as primary.
- **ArchiveFailing has no `for`.** The 5-minute `increase()` window already holds it for 5 minutes, so a `for` would only delay it.
- **NoPrimary does not fire in a normal failover.** That is intended. In a node failure, the old primary shows up as MemberDown, and FailoverOccurred records the promotion.

## Using it

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| List firing alerts | `make alerts` (`ALL=1 make alerts` adds pending ones). Reads Alertmanager through the API server's service proxy, with no port-forward and no exec |
| Prometheus UI | `make prometheus-ui`, then open http://127.0.0.1:9090 (Alerts, Status → Targets, Graph) |
| Alertmanager UI | `make alertmanager-ui`, then open http://127.0.0.1:9093 |
| Rule unit tests | `make test-alerts` (Docker only, no cluster) |
| Live checks | `make test-metrics`, `make alerts-failover`, `make alerts-archive` (`make test-l5` runs all four) |

The UI targets run `kubectl port-forward` in the foreground, bound to 127.0.0.1. Press Ctrl-C to stop. For a demo, run each in its own terminal. A useful query to show is the PromQL lag query above. To show live alerts, run `make alerts-archive` in another terminal and watch the Alerts page.

## Left out, and why

| Left out | Why |
|---|---|
| Grafana and dashboards (R10.4) | Out of scope by ADR-011 unless every MUST and SHOULD is done. The Prometheus UI and `make alerts` cover the demo. Listed in known limitations |
| A real notification receiver (email, Slack, webhook) | Would put a secret in a public repo. The receiver is a no-op, and wiring a real one is one block in `alertmanager.yml` |
| Persistent Prometheus storage | Metrics are for alerting, not history: 3 days in an emptyDir on the server node, lost if the pod moves. Alert `for` state is restored from the TSDB only while the pod lives |
| HA Prometheus or Alertmanager (2 replicas) | One server node (ADR-001). Losing the server node also loses the API server, a larger outage that the L2 API-outage test covers |
| Scraping `pg-restore` | A restored cluster is temporary and must not page. It is excluded at discovery and in every rule |
| cAdvisor, kubelet and API-server metrics | Not needed by any required alert. Pod memory comes from each process's own metrics |
| Log-based alerts (Loki and similar) | Every failure mode we alert on has a metric. Backup and restore Jobs signal failure by exit code |
| Connection, query and lock metrics (pg_stat_statements, long transactions) | Useful for tuning, but not required for HA or backups. The default exporter collectors still expose basic database statistics |
| Memory alert for database nodes | The restore test has a 1 Gi limit and each Postgres pod has a 1 Gi limit, so the kubelet enforces memory per pod. Host memory is shown in the resources table, not alerted on |

# L5 (ADR-011): Prometheus configuration. Only the pg-ha namespace is scraped for Postgres, so a restored
# cluster in pg-restore is never scraped. The alert rules are scoped to namespace="pg-ha" as well.
global:
  scrape_interval: 10s
  scrape_timeout: 5s
  evaluation_interval: 10s

alerting:
  alertmanagers:
    - static_configs: [{targets: ["alertmanager.monitoring.svc:9093"]}]

rule_files: [/etc/prometheus/rules/*.yml]

scrape_configs:
  # Patroni REST API /metrics on each member (role, timeline, streaming, sync standby).
  - job_name: patroni
    kubernetes_sd_configs:
      - role: pod
        namespaces: {names: [pg-ha]}
        selectors: [{role: pod, label: "app.kubernetes.io/name=pg"}]
    relabel_configs:
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_port_name], regex: patroni, action: keep}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_namespace], target_label: namespace}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name], target_label: pod}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name], target_label: node}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name], target_label: instance}

  # postgres_exporter sidecar on each member (pg_stat_archiver, custom pg_ha_* queries).
  - job_name: postgres
    kubernetes_sd_configs:
      - role: pod
        namespaces: {names: [pg-ha]}
        selectors: [{role: pod, label: "app.kubernetes.io/name=pg"}]
    relabel_configs:
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_port_name], regex: metrics, action: keep}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_namespace], target_label: namespace}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name], target_label: pod}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name], target_label: node}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name], target_label: instance}
    metric_relabel_configs:
      - {regex: server, action: labeldrop}     # always 127.0.0.1:5432, adds nothing

  # node_exporter DaemonSet (disk space, memory).
  - job_name: node
    kubernetes_sd_configs:
      - role: pod
        namespaces: {names: [monitoring-host]}
    relabel_configs:
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_port_name], regex: metrics, action: keep}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name], target_label: node}
      - {source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name], target_label: instance}

  # kube-state-metrics: Job, CronJob, StatefulSet and Deployment state in pg-ha and kube-system.
  # honor_labels keeps the object's own namespace label.
  - job_name: kube-state-metrics
    honor_labels: true
    static_configs: [{targets: ["kube-state-metrics.monitoring.svc:8080"]}]

  - job_name: alertmanager
    static_configs: [{targets: ["alertmanager.monitoring.svc:9093"]}]

  - job_name: prometheus
    static_configs: [{targets: ["localhost:9090"]}]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L5 (ADR-011): deploys Prometheus, Alertmanager, kube-state-metrics and node_exporter from deploy/monitoring
# with the pinned images, then waits until every scrape target is up. Idempotent. Part of make up.
# The postgres_exporter sidecar is part of the StatefulSet (scripts/deploy.sh), so it is not applied here.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
cluster_exists || die "cluster $CLUSTER_NAME not found, run: make cluster"
kubectl get ns "$PG_NS" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "namespace $PG_NS not found, run: make deploy"

kubectl kustomize "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/monitoring" |
  sed "s|__PROMETHEUS_IMAGE__|$PROMETHEUS_IMAGE|; s|__ALERTMANAGER_IMAGE__|$ALERTMANAGER_IMAGE|; s|__KUBE_STATE_METRICS_IMAGE__|$KUBE_STATE_METRICS_IMAGE|; s|__NODE_EXPORTER_IMAGE__|$NODE_EXPORTER_IMAGE|" |
  kubectl apply -f - | grep -v unchanged || true
for d in prometheus alertmanager kube-state-metrics; do kubectl -n monitoring rollout status "deployment/$d" --timeout=300s >/dev/null; done
kubectl -n monitoring-host rollout status daemonset/node-exporter --timeout=300s >/dev/null

# Every active target up, read through the API server's service proxy (no port-forward, no exec).
want=$((3 * 2 + $(kubectl get nodes --no-headers | wc -l) + 3))   # 3 members x 2 jobs, nodes, ksm + am + self
end=$((SECONDS + ${MON_WAIT:-180}))
while :; do
  t=$(kubectl get --raw /api/v1/namespaces/monitoring/services/prometheus:9090/proxy/api/v1/targets?state=active 2>/dev/null |
      jq -r '[.data.activeTargets[] | select(.health == "up")] | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  [ "$t" -ge "$want" ] && break
  [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || { kubectl get --raw /api/v1/namespaces/monitoring/services/prometheus:9090/proxy/api/v1/targets?state=active |
    jq -r '.data.activeTargets[] | "\(.labels.job) \(.labels.instance) \(.health) \(.lastError)"' >&2 || true; die "only $t of $want targets up"; }
  sleep 3
done
rules=$(kubectl get --raw /api/v1/namespaces/monitoring/services/prometheus:9090/proxy/api/v1/rules | jq '[.data.groups[].rules[]] | length')
log "Monitoring up: $t of $want targets up, $rules rules loaded. Alerts: make alerts. UIs: docs/observability.md"

content.content:
# Known limitations

This file lists what the system does not protect against or does not implement (R12.5, HC10). Entries are added as each phase confirms them.

## Topology

### Cluster DNS shares the server node's single point of failure

k3s runs one CoreDNS replica, and `make up` pins it to the server node (ADR-001, L3). A failed database node can no longer take DNS down. A server-node outage takes out the API server and DNS together, though. New connections by name (`pg-rw`, `pg-ro`, Garage) then fail, while existing connections and the running primary continue.

- **Why:** a single tainted server is the topology of ADR-001. Running CoreDNS on a database node made a node failure also a DNS failure, which pushed node-failure RTO over 30 s.
- **In production:** run at least two CoreDNS replicas spread across nodes or zones, or use NodeLocal DNSCache, on a control plane with three or more servers.
- **Decision:** ADR-001.

## Backups

### Backup repository is not off-site

The in-cluster Garage repository shares the VM and disk with the database, so it is not off-site disaster protection. In production, the pgBackRest repository points at GCS/S3 with bucket versioning and a retention lock, off-site from the cluster, using keyless workload identity where available.

- **Why it is the default:** `make up` must work for any reviewer with no cloud account or credentials.
- **Planned option:** R4.7 adds `BACKUP_TARGET=gcs make up`. It is OPTIONAL and not built yet.
- **Decision:** ADR-014.
8:**Yes, by planning estimate, this machine can run a 4-node local cluster (1 server, 3 agents) with 3 Postgres pods, Garage (ADR-014) and a plain Prometheus and Alertmanager stack.** Container networking now works. Memory limits are required and heavy tests must not overlap.
96:| Prometheus | 1.0 | 2.0 |

input.command:
cat >> docs/known-limitations.md <<'EOF'

## Monitoring

### No dashboards (R10.4 not met)

There is no Grafana and no dashboard as code. Metrics are viewed in the Prometheus UI (`make prometheus-ui`) and alerts with `make alerts` or the Alertmanager UI.

- **Why:** ADR-011 keeps Grafana out unless every MUST and every other SHOULD is done. It would serve only R10.4.
- **In production:** provision Grafana from code (datasource and dashboard JSON in ConfigMaps) next to Prometheus.
- **Decision:** ADR-011.

### Alerts are not delivered anywhere

Alertmanager routes every alert to a receiver with no integrations, so nobody is notified. Alerts are visible only through its API and UI.

- **Why:** a real receiver (webhook, Slack, email) needs a secret, and the repository is public.
- **In production:** add a receiver whose credential comes from a Secret created at deploy time, and route `critical` alerts to paging.
- **Decision:** ADR-011.

### Monitoring is a single, non-persistent instance on the server node

Prometheus and Alertmanager run as one replica each on the server node, with emptyDir storage (Prometheus keeps 3 days, at most 1 GB). A server-node outage stops alerting, and a pod restart loses metric history and pending alert state. FailoverOccurred compares the timeline with its value 5 minutes earlier, so it cannot fire in the first 5 minutes after Prometheus restarts.

- **Why:** one server node by design (ADR-001). Metrics serve alerting, not history.
- **In production:** two Prometheus replicas with persistent volumes and a clustered Alertmanager, ideally outside the database cluster, plus an external "dead man's switch" alert that pages when Prometheus itself goes silent.
- **Decision:** ADR-011.

### node_exporter runs with a Pod Security exception

node_exporter needs a read-only hostPath mount of the node's root filesystem to report disk space, which `baseline` and `restricted` forbid. It runs alone in the `monitoring-host` namespace, which enforces `privileged` and warns and audits at `restricted`. It runs as non-root with no capabilities, and without hostNetwork or hostPID.

- **Why:** disk space has no other source here. local-path volumes report no volume statistics.
- **Decision:** ADR-011, documented exception for R8.7.
EOF

input.new_string:
- **L6:** The API egress policy must allow the API server's **real backend IP and port**. Allowing only the Service IP stays blocked, so the address must be discovered at deploy time.

### Phase notes from L5

What L5 changes for L6 (security). Evidence is in `docs/evidence/L5-monitoring.md`. The design is in `docs/observability.md`.

- **NetworkPolicy ingress to `pg-ha`.** Prometheus in `monitoring` scrapes each member on 8008 (Patroni `/metrics`) and 9187 (exporter). Both ports must stay open to pods in `monitoring` with `app.kubernetes.io/name=prometheus`. Prometheus also needs 9100 to `monitoring-host`, 8080 and 8081 to kube-state-metrics, and 9093 to Alertmanager.
- **API server service and pod proxy.** `make alerts`, `make monitoring`, the L5 tests and the existing `patroni_cluster` helper all reach pods through the API server's proxy. That traffic comes from the server node, not from a pod. Ingress policies on 8008 (pg-ha), 9090 and 9093 (monitoring) must allow the server node's address, or these commands break. Check this with the S2 method before enforcing.
- **API egress.** Prometheus (pod discovery) and kube-state-metrics (list and watch) talk to the API server. Their egress policy needs the same real backend IP and port as Patroni (L4 note above).
- **TLS enforcement.** The exporter connects to `127.0.0.1:5432` with `sslmode=require` as `monitor`. It keeps working if `pg_hba` moves to `hostssl`, as long as a `127.0.0.1/32` line remains for `monitor`. The local socket allows `peer` only, which does not fit a role named `monitor`.
- **Patroni REST API is unauthenticated.** `/metrics` and `/cluster` are read without credentials. If L6 adds REST API TLS or auth, the `patroni` scrape job and `patroni_cluster` must change with it.
- **New identities for the R8.8 audit.** ServiceAccount `prometheus` gets pods get, list and watch in `pg-ha` and `monitoring-host`. ServiceAccount `kube-state-metrics` gets jobs, cronjobs, statefulsets and deployments list and watch in `pg-ha` and `kube-system`. Both are Roles, with no ClusterRole. Alertmanager and node_exporter mount no token.
- **Pod Security.** `monitoring` enforces `restricted`, and the `pg-ha` pods with the exporter sidecar are admitted under `restricted`. The only exception is `monitoring-host` (node_exporter, read-only hostPath), which enforces `privileged` and warns and audits at `restricted`.
- **Secrets.** The exporter reads the monitor password from the existing `pg-credentials` Secret through `secretKeyRef`. Alertmanager has no receiver secret.

**SHOULD cut lines**

# L5 history: monitoring and alerting

Hand-written notes for L5. The generated results are in [`L5-monitoring.md`](L5-monitoring.md). Times are UTC (the lead works in UTC+6). Session date 2026-11-25.

## Order of work

| Time (UTC) | Step |
|---|---|
| 16:14 | Start. Read CLAUDE.md, ADR-011, the L4 phase notes and versions.env |
| 16:20 | Step 0: the R5.5 note in `L4-restore-history.md` (11 timeline switches, 16 → 27) |
| 16:22 | postgres_exporter sidecar deployed with `make deploy`. **This rolled the three Postgres pods, before any measurement.** Patroni healthy at 16:23 |
| 16:31 | Monitoring stack deployed (`make monitoring`): 13 of 13 targets up, 19 rules |
| 16:32 | `make test-alerts` PASS on the first run, then three mutations checked by hand (below) |
| 16:35 | First `make test-metrics`: all checks PASS, but the harness killed itself on exit (bug 1 below). Fixed, then rerun at 16:53 |
| 16:39 | `make alerts-archive` PASS |
| 16:47 | `make alerts-failover` PASS |
| 16:53 | `make test-metrics` rerun with the fixes: PASS, exit 0 |

The monitoring stack was redeployed (Prometheus recreated) at 16:44 and again at 16:52 for small changes: kube-state-metrics' telemetry scrape, and the MemberDown summary text. Neither rolled the Postgres pods.

## Decisions taken during the phase

- **The exporter is a sidecar, not a central multi-target Deployment.** Each member is discovered with its pod and node labels, and the exporter dies with its member, so a stopped node shows as `up == 0` for that member. The cost was one rolling restart of the StatefulSet, done first.
- **The exporter connects over TCP to `127.0.0.1` with `sslmode=require`.** `pg_hba` allows the local socket for `peer` only, and the OS user (999) is not `monitor`. TLS keeps it working after L6 moves to `hostssl`.
- **Three custom exporter queries** (`--extend.query-path`): archive backlog, lag per standby, slot retention. The exporter logs that this flag is deprecated. It still works in v0.20.1. A future upgrade must check it.
- **ArchiveStale uses the oldest `.ready` age, not `last_archived_time`.** Seen live: the standbys report `pg_stat_archiver_last_archive_age` and non-zero `archived_count` from their earlier time as primary. Also, an idle primary closes no segment, so archive age grows with nothing at risk.
- **Two namespaces for monitoring.** Only node_exporter needs `hostPath`, so only `monitoring-host` enforces `privileged`. `monitoring` stays `restricted`.
- **Roles only, no ClusterRole.** Prometheus discovers pods in `pg-ha` and `monitoring-host` only. kube-state-metrics is limited to four resource types in `pg-ha` and `kube-system`.
- **An extra alert, MonitoringTargetDown,** was added beyond the requested list. The staleness alerts (backup, restore test, CoreDNS, disk) depend on kube-state-metrics and node_exporter, and would stay silent if those were down.
- **ReplicationLagHigh is two rules with the same name,** labelled `lag=bytes` and `lag=seconds`, so each has its own threshold and `for`.
- **The node's root filesystem is `overlay`** (a k3d node is a container). node_exporter's default `fs-types-exclude` drops overlay, so the exclude list was overridden. `mountpoint="/"` is then reported, and DiskLow uses it.

## Findings

1. **The CronJob's `lastSuccessfulTime` is not a backup signal.** `kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{cronjob="pg-backup"}` was 16:23 UTC, the time of the stanza-create Job. That Job and the check Jobs are made from the `pg-backup` template by `scripts/pgbr-job.sh` (`kubectl create job --from=cronjob/...`), so the CronJob owns them. BackupStale and RestoreTestStale therefore count only Jobs named `pg-backup-*` and `pg-restore-test*`. A unit test covers a fresh stanza Job alongside a stale backup. A side effect, not changed in L5: those owned Jobs also count toward the CronJob's `successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3`, so many check Jobs in one day can prune the last real backup Job. BackupStale would then fire early, a false alarm rather than a missed one.
2. **A full block cannot show the lag alert.** Blocking the stream ends the walsender after `wal_sender_timeout` (60 s), the `pg_stat_replication` row disappears, and ReplicaNotStreaming fires instead. `tc` is not in the k3s node image. An iptables `limit` match (40 packets/s, the rest dropped) slows the stream but keeps it connected. Lag reached about 218 MB and 120 s, and ReplicationLagHigh fired after its 2-minute `for`.
3. **NoPrimary does not fire in a node failover, by design.** The new primary held the lock 23 s after `docker stop`, inside NoPrimary's 45 s. The old primary showed up as MemberDown (pod `pg-2`). A second, namespace-level MemberDown instance came from the "fewer members up than replicas" branch. Its summary rendered an empty pod name, so it was given its own text.
4. **ArchiveFailing fires 77 s after the block, ArchiveStale 133 s after.** With dropped packets, pgBackRest's archive-push fails only after its io-timeout (about 60 s). ArchiveFailing resolved 424 s after the fault, about 5 minutes after the last failure, as its 5-minute window implies. ArchiveStale resolved 29 s after unblocking.
5. **Prometheus TSDB size.** About 1.2 MB of WAL after roughly 10 minutes, with about 4.5k head series. This has not been measured over a day. The 1 GB retention cap and the 2 Gi emptyDir limit bound it.

## Harness bugs found and fixed (no product impact)

1. `tests/l5-metrics.sh` cleanup ran `kill "${WRITER:-0}"` after `WRITER` had been cleared. `kill 0` signals the whole process group, so make printed `Terminated` (exit 143) after the test had already written PASS evidence. It now kills only a set PID. The run was repeated at 16:53 with exit 0. `tests/l5-alerts-archive.sh` had the same pattern and was fixed before its first real run.
2. `tests/l5-alerts-archive.sh` was created after the `chmod +x`, so the first `make alerts-archive` failed with `Permission denied` before doing anything.

## Mutation check of the unit tests (by hand, not committed)

Each mutation was applied to a scratch copy of the rules and `promtool test rules` was run against it.

| Mutation | Failing assertions |
|---|---:|
| NoPrimary `for: 45s` → `10s` | 1 |
| ArchiveStale `> 120` → `> 300` | 1 |
| BackupFailed/BackupStale without `namespace="pg-ha"` | 1 |

## exec and other disclosures (D4)

- **kubectl exec:** only through the existing `q` helper into the test client pod `pg-test-client`, from the committed L5 tests (WAL fills and archiver status). Never into a Postgres pod.
- **docker exec in committed fault scripts:** `iptables` on the primary's k3d agent in `tests/l5-metrics.sh` (stream throttle) and `tests/l5-alerts-archive.sh` (Garage block). Both are documented in the script headers, and both rules are removed on exit.
- **docker stop / start:** in `tests/l5-alerts-failover.sh`, as in `make failover-node`.
- **Ad hoc, outside committed scripts (read-only):** one `docker exec k3d-pg-ha-agent-0 sh -c 'which tc iptables ip; ...; ip route'`, to find out whether `tc` exists on the node image. Also `docker exec k3d-pg-ha-agent-N iptables -S FORWARD` on all three agents, to confirm that no test rule was left behind after the bug-1 exit. Neither changed anything.
- **Other ad hoc reads:** Prometheus queries through `kubectl get --raw` on the API server's service proxy.
- **Secrets:** no secret value was printed. The exporter reads the monitor password through `secretKeyRef`, and the evidence files pass through the existing `redact` filter.
